Theodoric, bishop of Metz, brother of the empress Cunigunda.

Adelbold, bishop of Utrecht.

Godefrid, duke, etc.

His brother Ethelo.

Otto, duke of Lorraine.

Albero, duke of the Mosellans.

Given on 17 May, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1012, indiction 10, concurrent 2, epact 24, and in the eleventh year of Emperor Henry.

Done successfully at Liège. Amen.

## LXVI. Emperor Henry grants the Bamberg Church the estate of Irnsing, situated in the district of Kelesgowe and in the county of Otto of Wittelsbach. (Year 1012, 1 November.)

[Ried, *Codex episcopatus Ratisbonensis*, I, 130.]

[Col. 0299D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRICUS, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, Roman emperor.

Let the diligence of all the faithful of Christ and of ourselves know how we, for the remedy of our soul and through the intervention of our most beloved wife, Chunigunda, empress Augusta, grant and donate, with the utmost and generous devotion, as a possession, a certain estate belonging to our jurisdiction called Eringesingun [Col. 0300A] (Irnsing), situated in the district of Kelesgowe and in the county of Count Otto, to the holy Bamberg Church, built and consecrated in honor of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and Saint George the martyr, together with all its appurtenances—namely, cultivated and uncultivated lands, villages, vineyards, fields, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, mills, plots, buildings, dependants of both sexes, outgoings and revenues—and with all the advantages that can either be written down or named.

This is on the condition that the venerable bishop of the same aforesaid holy Bamberg Church, Eberhard, and his successors thereafter have free power to hold and possess it and to do whatever pertains to the use of the aforesaid church, with every obstacle of opposition removed. If anyone, which God forbid, should presume to destroy the munificence of this donation of ours, let him pay for it with unquenchable torment on the day of judgment. To prevent this, and so that the authority of this donation of ours may remain stable and unshaken, we have ordered this charter to be written concerning it, have confirmed it with our own hand, and have commanded it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Augustus, Roman emperor. (Monogram.)

I, Guntherius, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain.

Given on the Kalends of November, indiction 3, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1012, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry II [Col. 0300C], and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Merseburg. Amen.

With the seal of majesty.

## LXVII. The privilege of Saint Henry for the monastery of Saint Benedict at Monte Cassino. (Year 1013.)

[Tosti, *History of the Abbey of Cassino*, I, 249.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRICUS, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, Roman emperor.

It is fitting for imperial greatness to heed the prayers of those who preside over persons serving God, and, out of love for the saints in whose honor their places have been dedicated—places where God’s flocks serve in divine warfare and strive to fulfill their duties—to comply willingly with what they request and to bestow gifts upon those places for the purpose of receiving divine recompense. The more diligently someone strives to accomplish this, the more, supported by God’s mercy, will he deserve both to pass more easily through the present life and to attain eternal blessedness.

Therefore, let the diligence of all the faithful of God’s holy Church and of ourselves, present and future, know [Col. 0301A] that the venerable abbot Atinulfus, instructed in the disciplines of the Rule and rector of the monastery of Saint Benedict, situated in the fortress of Cassino, where Saint Benedict himself consecrated with veneration the place of the burial of his body, together with the entire community which we know truly serves almighty God in that place under the Rule of the beneficent confessor Benedict, has petitioned our highness.

They asked that, for the honor of God and reverence for that holy place, for the increase of our soul, and for the stability of our kingdom, in accordance with the charters of our imperial predecessors—namely, the august emperors Charles, Lothair, and Otto—we might deign, by this charter of our authority, or rather of our confirmation, to confirm and strengthen for that venerable place the provisions written below [Col. 0301B]:

All the properties, possessions, dependants, and *aldianae*, registered servants, or servants and maidservants offered to it, together with lands and vineyards, woods, mountains, plains, level ground, waters and watercourses, and fisheries, situated within the boundaries of the principality of Pandulf of Capua and of Pandulf, prince of Benevento, with all the appurtenances that appear to lie within these boundaries and that we declare below, and whatever was possessed in ancient times.

Beginning at the first boundary, at Carnello itself, and following the way it rises through that place toward the stream called Siccus [lacuna] (the names of lands, churches, and other properties subject to the abbey follow) [lacuna] in its entirety, wherever they may be situated within the boundaries of our kingdom, and whatever came to the same venerable monastery of Saint Benedict, Christ’s confessor, and was possessed by it, or was held by it in any manner whatsoever: by this authority of our confirmation, the abbots of that monastery of Saint Benedict, present and future, shall firmly and inviolably hold and possess these things, insofar as the capacity or advantage of the venerable monastery requires.

Thus no judge, nor anyone exercising public judicial authority, shall dare to enter, in the present or future, into the cells and villages, fields or lands, places, or other possessions of the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict—those which it now justly and lawfully possesses in whatever districts and territories under the jurisdiction of our kingdom, or whatever divine piety may thereafter wish to add to that holy place—for the hearing of cases, the exaction of fines or taxes, the making of lodgings or requisitions [Col. 0301D], or for coercing servants, registered servants, or offered servants and those who reside on the land of that monastery. Nor shall anyone seek any payments or unlawful pretexts, or presume at any time to exact any of the matters mentioned above.

Rather, let the venerable abbot Atinulfus and his successors, together with the community serving God there, be permitted to live and reside peacefully under the protection of our safeguard, and to pray to God for our soul. Whatever the public treasury might by right have been able to expect from the aforesaid monastery’s property shall, for the recompense of our soul, remain granted by our authority to the lights of that most holy monastery [Col. 0302A].

Moreover, he also petitioned us, and we decided that it should be confirmed, that from all the properties or dependants belonging to that holy monastery—registered, offered, free, or servile—the portion of that monastery might more quickly obtain its justice. Thus, after an inquiry has been made, if they claim that a matter belongs to the aforesaid holy monastery through the truthful men named above, they shall be required to answer accordingly in the palace of whoever is concerned, or to respond under oath.

If a dispute should arise concerning servants or maidservants, or concerning any properties whatsoever, the monks of that holy monastery shall be permitted to retain them until they come into our presence or that of our successors, and there, when they have been brought before us, the matter shall be resolved.

Whoever attempts to act against this imperial [Col. 0302B] ordinance of ours, or fails to observe what has been mentioned above, or perhaps attempts to violate or break it, shall know that he must pay a penalty of one thousand pounds of the finest gold: half to our treasury, and half to the venerable abbot Atinulfus, or his successors, or the church of Saint Benedict.

We also order that wherever unlawful, harmful, or useless writings or claims concerning the properties or cells of that holy monastery are found, they be annulled or restored to the authority of Saint Benedict.

So that this imperial charter of ours may possess firmer force throughout future times, we have signed it below with our own hands and commanded it to be marked with our seal ring—perhaps, “to be distinguished by its impression.”

[Col. 0302C]

The sign of the lord Henry, most serene and invincible Augustus, emperor.

I, Heinricus, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Everardus, bishop and archchaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1013, indiction 12, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Rome. Amen.

## LXVIII. Saint Henry confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Bergamo, which had been badly treated by Bishop Reginfred. (Year 1013.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IV, 438.]

[Col. 0302D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HENRY, by the favor of divine clemency, king.

It is fitting for our excellence to regard the venerable places of the saints with a view to piety and, with careful consideration, to provide that those who serve God there suffer no injury. Therefore, let the diligence of all the faithful of God’s holy Church and of ourselves, present and future, know how Theoderulfus, archdeacon, on behalf of himself [and] all the others serving that same Church, came before our presence in the deepest grief and announced to us the misfortunes they had suffered in the territorial properties of their canonry at the hands of Bishop Reginfred and other evil men [Col. 0303A].

They humbly entreated our mercy that, for the remedy and salvation of our soul, they might be permitted, through the authority of our protection and the charter of our decree, to retain all the estates and properties belonging to the canonry of the blessed martyrs Alexander and Vincent—namely, the two markets granted by Adelbert, the most reverend pastor, and whatever else had been donated by him—as well as everything granted by Azo, the venerable bishop, or by other God-fearing men, according to the will of the donors.

Mercifully assenting to their petitions, as is just, by this charter of our decree we confirm and strengthen for them, subject to the honor of the bishop, all the properties and resources of the aforesaid canonry, as they have been set out above. This is on the condition that from now on they and their successors may have, hold, and firmly possess them for the use and benefit of those serving the holy Church, with all contradiction and claim by any person removed.

Therefore, ordering and decreeing, we establish that no duke, archbishop, bishop, margrave, count, viscount, gastald, nor any collector of public revenue, nor any great or small person of our kingdom, presume to dispossess, molest, or trouble the aforesaid canons, or their successors who in due course will serve God at the aforesaid venerable places of the saints, with respect to the properties written above.

If anyone, which we do not believe will happen, should prove a violator of this decree of ours, let him know that he must pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold: half, namely, to our treasury [Col. 0303C], and the other half to the aforesaid canons or their successors.

So that this may be believed more firmly and observed more diligently by everyone, we have confirmed this charter written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of the lord Henry, most invincible king.

I, Henry, have reviewed it in place of Everardus, bishop and archchaplain.

Done in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1013, indiction 11, in the eleventh year of the reign of the lord Henry II.

Done successfully at Magdeburg. Amen.

## LXIX. Saint Henry grants the estate of Berneshuson to the Paderborn Church. (Year 1013.)

[*Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae*, p. 62.]

[Col. 0303D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRICUS, by the favor of divine clemency, king.

Since the providence of divine disposition has raised us to govern at the summit of the commonwealth and has appointed us to preside over the multitude, although in merit we are inferior, nevertheless by a certain more exalted prerogative of name, it is necessary for us to obey in all things the commands of him by whose mercy we have been elevated. Thus, while providing for the welfare of our subjects, the more we are seen to have risen above others under the appearance of honor, the more inwardly humbled we should be, showing due recompense to those who serve under the shadow of our government and bending toward them with familiar compassion [Col. 0304A].

For if, examining the qualities of those who serve us with the attention of pious discernment, we strive to repay each according to the quality of his merits, by fulfilling our obligation we carry out the Lord’s command and fulfill the excellence of royal dignity.

We have seen fit to grant, with proprietary right, to the holy Paderborn Church, consecrated in honor of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of Saints Kilian the martyr and Liborius the confessor, a certain estate belonging to our property called Berneshuson, situated in the district of Lisga and in the county of Udo. We received it from Unewan, archbishop of Bremen, who donated it through his advocate Udo, by lawful transfer and without any legitimate opposition [Col. 0304B].

We grant it for the remedy of the souls of the divinely remembered Emperor Otto III, namely our lord, and all our parents, as well as our most beloved wife, and for the stability of the kingdom, together with all its appurtenances, properties, territories, villages, dependants of both sexes, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, roads and trackless places, outgoings and revenues, meadows and pastures, and with everything acquired or to be acquired.

This is on the condition that the aforesaid bishop and his successors have free power to turn it to the use and benefit of the same church. If anyone in the future, which God forbid, attempts to trouble the aforesaid church concerning these estates, let him be condemned by perpetual anathema. In addition, let him pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold, half to the royal treasury and the remaining [Col. 0304C] part to the same church which he presumed to trouble.

And so that the authority of this transfer of ours may remain stable, we have ordered this page of our royal charter to be written and, confirming it with our own hand, to be marked with our seal.

The sign of the lord Henry II, most invincible king. (L. M.)

Guntherius, chancellor, in place of Ercambald, archchaplain [has reviewed this]. [lacuna]

## LXX. Saint Henry confirms the privileges and possessions of the Paderborn Church. (Year 1014.)

[*Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae*, p. 63.]

[Col. 0304D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRICUS, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, Roman emperor.

Since the providence of divine disposition has raised us, through apostolic blessing, to govern the monarchy of the whole commonwealth, above all we must labor for this: that he who has granted us the crown of earthly empire may, after we have completed the span of this life, also permit us to be crowned with that which is not taken away forever.

We judge that this is accomplished especially if places devoted to ecclesiastical service are strengthened by our authority, so that, with every external disturbance removed, they may remain in tranquillity. In this way we may be helped by the prayers of those who are bound to devote themselves there, day and night, to prayer in God’s service, and may obtain through the pious intercession of those serving God’s holy Church what, I suppose, as men whose consciences are trembling, we do not presume to seek by ourselves [Col. 0305A].

Therefore, we wish it to be known to all the faithful of ourselves how Megenuvercus, the venerable bishop of the Paderborn Church, having undertaken arduous labor for the benefit of the Church, sought with us the thresholds of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul with pious intention. He came to make a devout petition that the Church over which he presides with pastoral care might first be strengthened by apostolic authority and then by our imperial authority, especially because, when the church was burned, all the charters and privileges of that church perished in the fire.

Since his petition appears reasonable, we freely assent to it. Whatever that same church ought justly to possess—whether by the donation of our predecessors or of ourselves, or by what other faithful people have granted to it in properties, territories, counties, or districts, or in any kinds of equipment, and whatever the aforesaid bishop Megenuvercus himself has bestowed there from his inheritance, or has legally acquired elsewhere through exchange or precarial grant—we again grant as a stable donation and confirm by imperial authority [Col. 0305B].

If anyone thereafter attempts with any presumption to violate the decree of our confirmation, let him be fined one hundred pounds of gold according to our weight and pay half to our treasury, and the remainder to the same church which he has rashly presumed to trouble.

And so that this confirmation may remain stable and unshaken through succeeding ages, we have ordered this page of the imperial charter to be written concerning it and, confirming it with our own hand, to be marked with our seal [Col. 0305C].

The sign of the lord Henry, most serene and invincible emperor. (L. M.)

I, Gunterius, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Ercanbald, archchaplain.

Given in indiction 11, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Pavia. Amen.

## LXXI. Saint Henry confirms to Peter, bishop and abbot of Saint Michael at Porcariana, his possessions and rights, in the year 1013, after the defeat of Arduino, invader of the kingdom of Italy; or certainly in the year 1014, before Easter, on which day, having received the insignia of empire from the Roman pontiff, he began to be emperor.

[In Acherius, *Spicilegium*, III, 386, from an ancient parchment of the archive of the Church of Besançon.]

[Col. 0305D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HENRY, by the favor of divine clemency, king.

While it is necessary for the government of each person to be guided by the reins of uprightness, the summit of royal honor ought to devote itself to the work of justice all the more generously and fully, and especially in the condition of the Catholic Church, the more it sees itself divinely exalted by the Lord.

Therefore, let the diligence of all the faithful of God’s holy Church and of ourselves, present and future, know that the lord Peter, a religious bishop and abbot of the monastery of Saint Michael [Col. 0306A], built in a place called Porcariana, came to the clemency of our piety and asked mercifully that, for the reward of eternal recompense and the remedy of our soul, we strengthen and confirm the aforesaid monastery, situated on the summit of a mountain, by the authority and stability of our charter.

Looking with favor toward his sacred prayers and hoping for future benefit, we confirm and strengthen by the protection of our charter the aforesaid monastery, together with the Alps and all the woods, fields, buildings, and other appurtenances situated on every side within a circuit of three miles around it.

We also confirm the castle and estate of Clavasce, which Margrave Hugo gave and transferred to that same holy and venerable place, for the remedy of his soul, with all its appurtenances, by a charter of his own donation; likewise Castaneto, Cacia [Col. 0306B], Breteneso, and Villarez, which is called Castello; Curtes, Maliasco, and Sablonem; and the other properties which Margrave Arduino, son of Otto, gave to the aforesaid monastery, together with its cells, churches, and all other movable and immovable property which it now appears to possess and which God may wish to increase there in the future.

We confirm and strengthen these things by our charter for the aforesaid abbot, for the holy community serving God in that place, and for their successors; and, insofar as we can justly and lawfully do so, we establish and strengthen them on the following condition: that the abbot, the community entrusted to him, and their successors shall have, hold, and firmly possess the monastery in its entirety, inwardly and outwardly [Col. 0306C], without disturbance, opposition, or diminution by us, our successors, or any other person.

Moreover, we grant and bestow upon the community of that holy place permission to elect an abbot proven in conduct and adorned with the commandments of Christ and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

Therefore, ordering and commanding, we establish by this authority of our charter that no duke, archbishop, bishop, margrave, count, viscount, *sculdascius*, gastald, nor any great or small person of our kingdom presume to trouble, molest, or dispossess the aforesaid monastery, its abbots, or its community; nor to take fodrum, impose a legal obligation, or hold a court, unless the abbot of that place or his agents should presume to do so [Col. 0306D].

If anyone should prove a violator of this charter of our strengthening, let him know that he must pay one thousand pounds of the finest gold: half to our treasury and half to the abbot and his successors.

So that this may be believed more firmly and observed by everyone both now and in the future [lacuna], we have confirmed it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

## LXXII. Diploma of Emperor Henry II for the monastery of Saint Saviour at Fontana Taonis. (Year 1014.)

[Zaccaria, prefect of the Este library, *Anecdota medii aevi*, part III, p. 218, from the archive of the Vallombrosan Fathers of Pistoia.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HENRY [Col. 0307A], by the generosity of divine clemency, Augustus, Roman emperor.

It seems just and reasonable to us that the venerable places of God’s saints, which good men, out of regard for piety and hope of an eternal reward, bestow and transfer to our right and dominion, should be placed under the protection of our authority.

Therefore, we wish it to be known to the whole body of the faithful of God’s holy Church and of ourselves, present and future, how we have received under the protection of our imperial safeguard the monastery of Saint Saviour, situated at Fontana Tanoni, which Margrave Boniface granted to it, for the remedy of his soul, by proprietary right: namely, the estates called Cafadia Bonifacinga, and the village called Stazano with all its appurtenances, and everything he possessed in the *badium* [uncertain term], which he likewise donated to it.

We have received these and whatever else it may be able to acquire in the future with God’s help under the protection of our safeguard, and we wish them to remain perpetually, quietly and peacefully, under our defense, without anyone’s molestation [Col. 0307B].

We decree that from this hour onward no duke, margrave, bishop, count, viscount, gastald, *sculdascius*, dean, or any great or small person of our empire dare dispossess, molest, or trouble the monk John, abbot, who serves God there, or the other monks who are now there or who in due course serve God in that place, without a judgment of the imperial legate.

If anyone should prove a violator of this imperial safeguard, let him know that he must pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold: half to our treasury [Col. 0307C], and half to the aforesaid abbot John, to the brothers, and to their successors.

So that this may be believed more firmly and observed more diligently by everyone, we have ordered it to be marked with our seal.

I, Henry, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Everardus, bishop and archchancellor.

Place of the seal.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction 12, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus [Note: [Col. 0307D] Unless one prefers to suppose that an error has entered into the reckoning of the years, and that “the twelfth year of the reign” was written instead of the thirteenth, one should say that the diploma was issued before the Kalends of March in the year 1014. Then everything will flow properly. For—as Muratori demonstrates concerning this year against Pagi and others—around March of the year 1014, Henry II took possession of the kingdom of Italy.] and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Papiano. Amen.

## LXXIII. Henry II, king of Germany, confirms the privileges of the Arimanni of Mantua. (Year 1014.)

[Muratori, *Antiquitates Italicae*, IV, 13.]

[Col. 0307D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HENRY, by the favor of divine clemency, king.

Let the keen understanding of all the saints of God and of our faithful, present and future, know how we, for the love of God and the remedy of our soul, have granted and strengthened by this charter of our decree, insofar as we can justly and lawfully do so, all the Arimanni residing in the city of Mantua, whether in the fortress called Portus or in the villages called San Giorgio, Cepada, and Formigosa, or in the county of Mantua.

We grant them all their inheritance, whether held by paternal or maternal right, their property, communal holdings, and all things possessed by their parents and acquired or to be acquired by them—specifically, the woods of Armanore, Carpeneta, Succa, and Septingenti, and those lying in the other places in the Mantuan county—together with fisheries, rivers, and marshes, even without any written title, insofar as these things justly and lawfully pertain to them; together with families of both sexes, servants and maidservants, holders of *libelli*, holders of precarial grants, and all their movable and immovable property.

Their boundaries are as follows: both banks of the river Tartar, then upstream as far as the river Oglio; on the other side, the Fossa Alta; on the third side, the church of Saint Faustinus at the head of Variana, and from there separately as far as Agricia Maior [Col. 0308B].

We grant them, moreover, exemption from all toll and river dues that they incur in carrying on commerce at Garda, Lasese, and the upper lake, or at Brescia, Ferrara, Comacchio, and Ravenna. They, their sons, and the men who conduct commerce while working on their behalf shall have the power and permission to trade throughout the aforesaid lake, without contradiction from anyone, public levy, or payment of any toll or river due.

Therefore, ordering and commanding, we establish that from now on no duke, bishop, margrave, count, viscount, gastald, *sculdascius*, dean, or any great or small person of our kingdom presume to trouble, dispossess, or molest the aforesaid Arimanni with regard to their persons or any of the properties mentioned above. No one may lodge in their residences against their will, compel them to perform any public service except one which their predecessors performed according to law, or do anything without a lawful judgment [Col. 0308C].

If anyone, which we do not believe will happen, should rise against this decree of ours or attempt to violate it, let him know that he must pay one thousand pounds of the finest gold: half to our treasury and half to the aforesaid Arimanni residing and dwelling in the said city of Mantua, in the fortress of Portus, or in the Mantuan county.

So that this may be believed more firmly and observed more diligently by everyone, we have ordered it to be marked below with the impression of our seal.

[Col. 0308D]

The sign of the lord Henry, most invincible king.

I, Henry, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Everardus, bishop and archchaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction 12, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry II.

Done successfully at Ravenna. Amen.

## LXXIV. Saint Henry confirms and enlarges the privileges of the Hamburg Church. (Year 1014.)

[In Lappenberg, *Hamburgische Urkunden*, p. 64.]

[Col. 0309A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRICUS, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, Roman emperor.

If we bring the pious petitions of priests to fulfillment with willing devotion, we undoubtedly believe that this will benefit us both for the condition of the present life and for obtaining the rewards of eternal blessedness.

Therefore, let the diligence of all our faithful, present and future, know how the venerable Unaco, archbishop of the Hamburg Church, whom we appointed over that Church, caused the charters of blessed memory, our lord and predecessor Otto III, Augustus, emperor, to be presented before our sight [Col. 0309B]. These charters contained how Otto, for the love of God, had granted by imperial authority liberty and protection to the monasteries situated in his bishopric. Unaco also asked our highness that we should once again confirm by our decree those monasteries and everything belonging to them.

We, therefore, granting assent to his just and reasonable petition, through the intervention of our beloved consort, namely Chunigunda, empress Augusta, and in honor of holy Mary, Mother of God, to whom that place, Hamburg, is consecrated, grant to that Hamburg place and to the other monasteries belonging to this diocese—namely, Bremen, Bucken, Ramesloh, Birken, Heslingen, and Ripesholt [Col. 0309C]—whatever my lord and predecessor, and his predecessors, namely kings and emperors, had granted to those monasteries by donation or confirmation.

This is on the condition that they shall always remain perpetually under our protection, with all their appurtenances, whether acquired or to be acquired.

Moreover, we grant to the aforesaid archbishop and his successors permission to establish a market in the place called Bremen, where the archbishopric is now situated, together with the ban, toll, and a public coinage of pure silver according to the public standard. Whatever is recognized as belonging from this to our treasury, we confer upon the aforesaid Bremen see.

Furthermore, we grant the merchants who are inhabitants of that place the patronage of our protection [Col. 0309D], ordering by this decree of imperial authority that they enjoy in every respect such protection and right as the merchants of the greater cities throughout our kingdom are known to enjoy. No one shall claim any authority there except the archbishop of the aforesaid see and the advocate whom he chooses.

In addition, we order by imperial decree that no duke, margrave, count, or any other judicial authority presume to usurp any power over the people of the aforesaid monasteries—Hamburg, Bremen, Bucken, Ramesloh, Birken, Heslingen, and Ripesholt—or over their other appurtenances.

Nor shall anyone constrain the *liti*, colonists, or *jamundlingi* by a ban of the head for theft of the head, or by any other ban, or compel them to render any justice, except through the advocates of the aforesaid archbishop, whom he himself wishes and appoints as advocates [Col. 0310A]. Those advocates, however, shall constrain the aforesaid people by our ban to render every lawful service.

So that this donation of ours may be believed more firmly by the faithful of God and of ourselves and observed more carefully, unshaken throughout future times, we have ordered this charter to be written, strengthened with our hand, and marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of the lord Henry II, most glorious Augustus, emperor. (M.)

I, Guntherius, chancellor, have reviewed it in place of Gumbaldus, archchaplain. (S.)

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, indiction 12, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014 [Col. 0310B], in the thirteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Altstedt.

## LXXV. Saint Henry confirms the privileges of the Treviso Church. (Year 1014.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, V, 508.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, I, HEINRY, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, emperor.

If, while devoutly serving the Churches, we grant them what they request, we do not doubt that we shall undoubtedly receive the reward of eternal recompense.

Therefore, let the whole body of the faithful of God’s holy Church and of ourselves, present and future, know that Arnaldus, venerable bishop of the holy Treviso Church, through the intervention and petition of Egilbert, bishop of the Church of Freising [Col. 0310C], implored our imperial highness that, for the love of God and the remedy of our soul, we might confirm to him and to his Church, by this charter of ours, all the charters established and confirmed by our predecessors.

Granting assent to his worthy petitions and observing the charters of our predecessors, we confirm and strengthen for him and for his church all the charters of our predecessors, whether kings or emperors, and the matters contained in them—namely, two parts of the toll and market dues of the port of Treviso, together with the district and lawful jurisdiction; likewise two portions of the public coinage; and also the toll of the aforesaid city, within and without, as it has hitherto come under our authority, both from Christians [Col. 0310D] and from Jews who have undertaken to conduct business there.

We confirm all these things in their entirety to the aforesaid Church of Treviso. We also confirm Saint Mary with the castle of Asylo and all its appurtenances, as well as the monastery of Crespulinus, or the abbey of Saint Hilary, with its ecclesiastical district; likewise the tithes of grain and beer, and all other things known to have been donated and granted to the aforesaid holy Church by God-fearing people through chartered instruments.

Even if, when danger from fire or some other misfortune threatened, that Church lost the aforesaid charters or other writings through negligence, we confirm and strengthen these possessions for it by this charter of our authority, so that the bishop of that Church may hold, order, and dispose of those properties [Col. 0311A], together with all their movable and immovable goods, without contradiction or molestation by anyone.

If anyone, therefore, attempts with wicked boldness to violate this charter of our confirmation, let him know that he must pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold: half to our treasury and half to the aforesaid Church and its rectors.

So that this may be believed more firmly and observed more diligently, we have ordered it, confirmed by our own hand, to be marked with our seal.

The sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Augustus, emperor.

I, Gumherius, chancellor, have recorded it in place of Harconbaldus, archchaplain.

[lacuna] of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction 11, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, most serene emperor [Col. 0311B], and in the first year of his empire.

Done in the village of Dulceri [lacuna].

Place of the seal.

### LXXVI. Saint Henry restores to Peter, bishop of Novara, the rights of his church, taken away by Margrave Arduino. (Year 1014)

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, IV, 700.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the divinely ordained clemency, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

When we grant assent to the petitions of the faithful addressed to our imperial majesty, we have no doubt that they will thereby become more ready and devoted to our service. Therefore, let the prudent knowledge of all the faithful of the Catholic Church and of our own people, both present and future, recognize that Peter, the venerable man, bishop of the holy Church of Novara and our faithful servant, who endured many hardships on account of his loyalty to us—namely hunger, thirst, heat, and cold—and, with his enemies pursuing him, crossed icy rocks and very rugged hills barefoot while fleeing, has now also suffered many losses because of Arduino’s devastation. For its churches have been plundered, its castles broken apart, its houses overthrown, its vineyards cut down, its trees stripped of bark; moreover, its parishes and estates have been given by Arduino as benefices to his enemies.

He has therefore approached our imperial excellence so that, in compensation for his labor and restoration of his losses, we might grant to the aforesaid Church of Novara a certain small county which is known to lie in the valley of the Ausula, within the parish of that bishopric, together with all the public revenues belonging to that county. He has also entreated us to restore to his Church a parish of his bishopric which, long ago, through evil procedure and unjust action, his church lost—situated in a village called Trecate, not very far from the city—and also the estate called Gravalona, formerly belonging to that bishop, but now known to have been unjustly seized.

It is therefore fitting that the aforesaid prelate should receive from us a reward for his labor. And since it is just that the parish mentioned above and the aforesaid estate should be restored to their bishopric, and that other faithful men of ours, on learning this, should be more firmly established in loyalty to us, granting his petitions, we wholly transfer and grant the said small county from our jurisdiction into the power of his church. By this decree of our authority we return and grant the aforesaid parish and estate to the aforementioned Church of Novara, together with all jurisdiction, tolls, and fisheries located in the River Toxo, specifically in those places where that Church holds land on both sides of the river; together with hunting rights and all things that can be exacted from the same county for the public treasury; with chapels, a house, a small court, farmsteads, cottages, dwelling-sites, fields, meadows, vineyards, pastures, woods, stables, saltworks, marshes, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, cultivated and uncultivated lands, divided and undivided lands, the boundaries of the grant, fishponds, field dues, and all other revenues; with male and female slaves, male and female dependants of half-free status, and all things that can be named or called as belonging or pertaining to the aforesaid parish or estate.

We also grant the port of Bestamo belonging to the same parish, which our glorious uncle Otto the Great granted to the aforesaid see by decree. Thus no margrave, count, viscount, his sculdascius, or any person, great or small, shall dare to distrain the men of the aforesaid county, parish, or estate, or presume to exact anything within that county, impose compulsory services, or acquire any revenues. Rather, let the aforesaid prelate and his successors be permitted to hold the aforementioned county together with the aforesaid parish and estate, and to distrain all the men of that county or of that parish or estate, either personally or through their legate, just as they would be distrained by us or by our envoy; and let him have all things belonging to the public treasury from that county or capable of being exacted from it, together with the aforesaid parish of Trecate and estate of Gravalona, with all their appendages and dependencies.

Let him and his successors—those who, with God’s favor, will assume the administration and chair of that see—have, hold, and firmly possess these things, with all contradiction, diminution, or interference by us, our royal and imperial successors, or any person removed.

If anyone should presume, with wicked and rash intent, to violate this decree of our grant and confirmation, let him be compelled to pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold: one half to our palace and the other half to the Church of Novara and its rector who shall at that time be in charge there. And so that this may be believed more truly and observed more diligently by all, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

**Sign of the lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Issued in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction XII, in the thirteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Trucuiana. Amen.

---

### LXXVII. Saint Henry confirms and enlarges the possessions of the Church of Savona. (Year 1014)

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, IV, 732.]*

#### [Col. 0313A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, ever Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

Divine providence has raised us to imperial dignity and adorned us with the summit of such power so that we may always be vigilant and attentively concerned for divine worship, and for the protection, defense, and authority of the Church of Christ. Therefore, let the knowledge of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own people, present and future, know how Ardeman, bishop of Savona, presented before our imperial presence a decree and a charter of protection belonging to our predecessors, the most noble emperors Otto, showing how those emperors had granted to the aforesaid Church of Savona possessions, estates, and immunities.

Accordingly, considering their confirmations—namely, the decree and the charter of protection—we, for the love of God and the salvation of our soul, confirm and firmly strengthen forever by this our imperial decree the house with tower, court, and dwellings, the gate and bank of the said castle of Savona, and, moreover, the Round Lake, Cardeto, Manduculo of Callo, Cairo, Casale Grasso, Eremana, Aqua Marcia, and as much land at Ponte as belongs to Saint Eugene; Monte Curro, Valla in Asti; one tunicella; the parish of Saint Donatus; the parishes of Melosina, Saint Mary at Gugada, and Manarate; Sale, Monte Bar, Cario, Corgenio, Leone, Scrunito, Lavaniola—which is called Dry Gausa—Saliceto, Camariana, Saint Julia, Viniale, Cinglo, Cruce Ferie, Boile, Cairo, Deco, Salsole, Plana, and Bruvio.

Together with those same courts, parishes, and properties, with their tithes, chapels, vineyards, servants of both sexes, lands, meadows, fields, pastures, and woods, and with all their own courts, tithes, and revenues, we wholly confirm them to Aldeman, bishop of Savona, and to his successors.

We therefore order and command that no duke, margrave, count, or any person, great or small, of our empire presume to dispossess or molest the aforesaid see of Savona with respect to the aforementioned possessions.

If anyone does so, let him pay one hundred pounds of gold: one half to our treasury and the other half to the aforesaid Bishop Aldeman and his successors. And so that this may be believed more truly, we have strengthened this document with our own hand and ordered it to be sealed.

**Sign of the lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Henry, chancellor, acting in place of Everard, bishop and archchaplain, has examined and authenticated this document.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction XII, in the fifth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus.

Done successfully at Pavia. Amen.

---

### LXXVIII. Henry, out of regard for Bishop Ardeman, confirms the possessions of the people of Savona. (Year 1014)

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, IV, 734.]*

#### [Col. 0314A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

We wish it to be known to all our faithful, present and future, how, at the intervention of Ardeman, bishop of Savona and our beloved faithful servant, by the authority of our decree we grant, confirm, and strengthen for all the principal men dwelling in the marquisate of Savona, in the castle, all their possessions and properties from the Sea-Mountain and beyond it, together with their leaseholding villages, fisheries, and hunting rights, which they have customarily possessed.

Moreover, we order that no castles be built within the boundaries prescribed above, nor any burden be imposed upon the aforesaid men by the margraves, their counts, or their viscounts—namely, a levy, the seizure of men, or the destruction of houses.

Therefore we commend and firmly establish forever that no duke, margrave, bishop, count, viscount, gastald, huntsman, or any person, great or small, of our empire presume to disturb or molest the aforesaid men dwelling in the castle of Savona with respect to the possessions described above.

If anyone should attempt to violate or break this imperial decree, let him know that he must pay one thousand pounds of the finest gold: one half to our treasury and the other half to the noble men described above who dwell in the castle of Savona.

And so that this may be believed more truly and observed more diligently by all, we have strengthened it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our imperial seal.

**Sign of the lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Henry, chancellor, acting in place of Everard, bishop and our chaplain, has examined and authenticated this document.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction XII, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully in the palace at Pavia.

---

### LXXIX. The privilege of Saint Henry for the monastery of Saints Peter, Lawrence, and Columbanus, “which is called Bromiades.” (Year 1014)

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, 983.]*

#### [Col. 0314D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

If, at the petition of God’s servants, we relieve ecclesiastical necessities by our assistance and protect them with imperial defense, we faithfully believe that this will benefit us both in passing through mortal life in time and in obtaining eternal life happily in the future.

Therefore, let it be known to all our faithful, present and future, how the venerable man Constantius, abbot of the monastery of Saints Peter, Lawrence, and Columbanus, which is called Bromiades, approached the serenity of our majesty, asking that the possessions of that monastery, together with the people subject to it, should remain under the protection of our immunity, and that we should make them free and exempt from every public service and judicial exaction.

We willingly granted his petition, out of affection for the aforesaid [person] and reverence for Blessed Peter the Apostle, Lawrence, and Columbanus. By this document of our authority, in accordance with the decrees of our predecessors, namely the kings and emperors Charles, Louis, Lothair, Hugh, and the three Ottos, we decree that all the possessions of the aforesaid monastery, together with its cells and the people subject to it, shall in every respect remain under the protection of our defense.

Finally, we confirm and strengthen to the said monastery all its possessions, estates, villages, churches, cells, farmsteads, and families of both sexes, as well as the first fruits and tithes of all the people cultivating the land of that abbey, just as these have been granted and confirmed there by the privileges of the Roman pontiffs or by the decrees of kings and emperors.

This includes the land it possesses in the county of Modena, in the place and estate called Plagassano, with the chapel of Saint Columbanus built there and the revenues it possesses there, and at Salsina; in the county of Parma, at a place called Caselle, and at Beneseto, Farigari, Galemano, and Solignano; and in the county of Volterra, one small estate called Frigesimum, with all its appurtenances, whether in these or in any other counties or places.

It includes houses, dwelling-sites, fields, vineyards, meadows, pastures, woods and stables, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, hunting rights, mountains, valleys, Alps, plains, cliffs and crags, male and female slaves, male and female dependants of half-free status, markets, tolls, and all things belonging to the aforesaid abbey—both those which it now appears to possess and those which divine mercy may hereafter wish to add or increase.

Just as our predecessors have always protected this same monastery, so we command that it remain kept apart from all enemies and invaders, defended and fortified by our imperial protection.

We therefore establish, order, and command that no public judge or any administrator of the state of higher rank presume to enter the churches, villages, or other possessions which the monastery now justly and legally holds in any provinces or territories of our empire in order to hear cases according to judicial procedure. Nor may anyone take feudal dues, taxes, lodging, tolls, or sureties; distrain free or enslaved persons dwelling upon the land of the monastery; or dare to seek any public services, revenues, or unlawful pretexts.

Rather, with the opposition and disturbance of all persons removed, let the aforesaid abbot and his successors be permitted to possess peacefully, under the protection of our defense, the possessions of the monastery and the people belonging to it, and continually to implore the immense mercy of the Lord for our safety and for the stability of our empire, together with the clergy and monks entrusted to them.

And so that this authority of ours may retain inviolate and unshaken firmness in future times, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring. If anyone should presume to violate it, let him know that he must pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold: one half to the aforesaid monastery, against which he committed the violence, and the other half to our treasury, while this inscription of ours remains unshaken.

**Sign + of the lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Henry, chancellor, acting in place of Luitard, bishop and archchancellor, has examined and authenticated this document.

Given on the Nones of May, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction XII, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Pavia, in the palace at Ticinum, in the name of God. Amen.

---

### LXXX. The decree of Saint Henry by which he protects the Church of Worms against the unjust demands of the provincial counts. (Year 1014)

*[Schannat, Episcopatus Wormatiensis, II, 40.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the divinely preordained clemency, Augustus, emperor.

If we bring to fulfillment the petitions of God’s priests concerning the needs of the churches entrusted to them, which they report to our attention, we confidently believe that this will unquestionably benefit us both for the stability of our temporal kingdom and for the increase of eternal blessedness.

Therefore, let the knowledge of all the faithful of God and of ourselves, present and future, know how the venerable man Burchard, bishop of the holy Church of Worms, approached our majesty, together with the common lament of the bishops and abbots of that province, lodging a complaint about the frequent injury and unjust law imposed by our counts upon the entire household of his Church through their presumption.

The law was that whenever anyone from that household was found guilty of theft, fighting, or any criminal matter, whether the matter were great or small, he was always required to pay sixty solidi to the count.

Among other things, he also presented for our inspection decrees of immunity which the most Christian king of the Franks, Dagobert, had first granted to God and to his holy apostles Peter and Paul. These decrees stated how Dagobert had established that no count should have any authority to hear cases concerning that household.

He also showed us the confirmations of Dagobert’s successors—namely Pippin, Charles, Louis, Arnulf, Henry, and the three Ottos, the distinguished kings and emperors who were our predecessors. In these we found that they had renewed the constitution of the aforesaid King Dagobert by their own decrees. Since he wished this unjust law not to continue any further, he entreated our clemency to restrain the presumptuous attacks of the counts by our authority and to confirm anew, by our authority, the possessions of his church.

Granting his petitions out of love for divine worship and for his willing service, we have decreed that this order of our majesty be issued to the same church. By it we command that the aforesaid Bishop Burchard and his successors, just as the aforementioned kings and emperors established and confirmed, should possess all the property of their church peacefully, and that our counts should henceforth presume to inflict no injury or injustice upon the household of that church.

Furthermore, for the reward of eternal blessedness and in reverence for the blessed Peter and Paul, we establish this imperial decree and command that it remain stable and firm forever:

If anyone from the household of the Church of Worms should henceforth commit theft, engage in fighting, or perpetrate any other criminal act within that household, he shall make compensation into the hands of the bishop through his advocate.

If, however, he has a quarrel with some outsider beyond the household, his advocate shall render justice to the count on his behalf. If he commits any injustice against a free man, fights with him, or carries out any abduction beyond the household, his advocate shall likewise render justice on his behalf.

If he commits any theft within another person’s enclosure, he shall return and restore what he took and shall additionally pay five solidi. If he commits theft outside it, he shall again restore what he took and shall pay only one ounce in compensation; he shall never be liable for a greater pledge than five solidi.

The counts shall have absolutely no authority over the household of the aforesaid Church except in a lawful court, when, with the judgment of the scabini and the oath of free men, someone within it is proved to be a thief. If he is openly caught in theft, he shall meanwhile be held in the count’s fetters until he is justly judged in the count’s court according to the judgment of the scabini.

As for the sixty solidi which they have until now received under an unjust and unreasonable law, we entirely prohibit them from receiving them, except in public cities.

If anyone violates the decrees of this confirmation or becomes a transgressor of our constitution, then, if he is free, let him pay three pounds of gold to our treasury; but if he is a slave, let him lose his hide and hair.

But so that this authority may remain firm and stable forever, we have written it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of August, indiction XII, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1014, in the thirteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, and in the first year of his empire.

Done successfully at Mersfelt, in the name of God.

---

### LXXXI. The letter of Saint Henry by which he grants the abbey of Schwarzach to Werenharius, bishop of Strasbourg, and his successors for possession. (Year 1014)

*[Gallia Christiana, V, Instrumenta, 469.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, king.

#### [Col. 0318A]

Since, according to the rational order established by almighty God, the form of the human body was created in such a way that its lesser members are subject to the head and are governed by it as by a leader, we have thought it not inappropriate to imitate this arrangement by subjecting certain lesser churches in our kingdom to greater ones. We have judged that this does not conflict with the will of the King of kings, who knows how to distinguish heavenly and earthly principalities according to a wondrous order.

Therefore, we too, who have been chosen to reign for a time under the eternal King, have done the following: first, for the love of God and of his Mother; also because of the constant petitions of our beloved wife Cunegund; because of the faithful counsels of Heribert, archbishop of Cologne, and of his brother Becelo, bishop of Würzburg; likewise on the advice of our brother Bruno of Augsburg; at the request and with the consent of our other faithful; and indeed because of the continual service of Werenharius, bishop of Strasbourg—we have handed over an abbey of monks called Suazaha, founded in honor of the Mother of God, to the holy Church of Strasbourg, to be possessed perpetually in memory of ourselves and our successors.

We grant it together with everything legally belonging to that abbey in whatever provinces, both movable and immovable: lands, buildings, male and female slaves, cultivated and uncultivated lands, fields, meadows, pastures or common pastures, vineyards or vine-plots, woods, forests, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, roads and trackless places, entrances and exits, and all other equipment.

The aforesaid Bishop Werenharius and his successors shall thereafter have free authority over this abbey, without contradiction or molestation by any person, to possess it and to do with it in every way whatever they wish for the uses of the Church.

And so that the authority of this grant of ours may remain stable and unshaken, this page of our decree, according to royal custom, [lacuna]; and, after it had been written out, we strengthened it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

**Sign of the lord Henry, unconquered king.**

Suncelinus, chancellor, acting in place of Erchanbold, archchaplain, has examined and authenticated this document.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February, Tuesday, on the fourth day of the moon, in the year from the Lord’s incarnation 1014, indiction XII, in the twelfth year of the reign of the lord Henry, king.

Done at Pavia.

---

### LXXXII. The sentence of Saint Henry against the counts and margraves of Este, who refused to obey his imperial command. (Year 1014)

*[Lunig, Codex diplomaticus, I, 1523.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

We wish it to be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God that Count Ubertus, son of Hildeprand; Margrave Otbertus and his son; and Albert, his grandson, after electing us king and emperor, and after giving us their hands and making oaths to us, invaded our kingdom together with Arduino, the enemy of God and of us.

They committed robberies, plundering, and devastation everywhere; and, what cannot be said without grief, they stripped the territories and dependencies of all the churches miserably of all their goods.

Great grief, excessive mourning, unheard-of desolation within and without! If, however, the churches thus destroyed are aided, whatever pleases God will please no good person less.

Therefore, after taking counsel with the friends of God, we searched out and found the law of the Lombards, which commands as follows:

> “If anyone should plot against the king’s life, or should have given counsel against his life, let him incur danger, and let his possessions be confiscated.”

According to their law, therefore, all their goods are our property, since it is manifest that they not only plotted or gave counsel against us, but also carried out their wicked audacity and impious attempts in action and openly prepared wars against us.

Since, therefore, according to their laws their goods are ours, we wish to give a portion of their estates to the Church of Saint Cyrus, bishop of Ticinum, which they have violently devastated in its dependencies with fire and plunder. Thus, with some compensation made, it may be able to endure more tolerably the losses inflicted upon it until, by God’s gift, greater advantages accrue to it.

Accordingly, justly and legally, from the possessions of Ubertus, son of Hildeprand, we give it the castle of Cerreto and Vulparia, with all their dependencies, extending to one thousand jugera, together with all their jurisdiction.

From the possessions of Ubertus [read: Otbertus] and his sons, and of Albert, their grandson, the margrave, we give it whatever they appear to have possessed at Scadrampo near the castle of Balbiano, and in the territory of Saint Martin at Strata and at Casale, extending to five hundred jugera.

Thus the Church of the most blessed confessor of the Lord, Cyrus, and the pastor who shall be there from time to time, shall possess and administer forever, by right of ownership, all the things named above with their dependencies—waters and watercourses, banks, mills, fisheries, cultivated and uncultivated lands, woods, channels, fords, hunting rights, stables, male and female slaves, chapels, mountains and valleys, cliffs and meadows, markets and jurisdictions, and everything that can be named—with all contradiction, molestation, or diminution by us, our successors, or anyone else removed.

Moreover, we grant to Saint Cyrus, our patron, the jurisdiction of Secema for eight miles in every direction around it, insofar as it appears to belong to our share, for the peace and quiet of that Church and for the remedy and salvation of our soul and of the souls of our successors, kings and emperors.

If anyone should attempt to act against this decree of ours, which, with God’s favor, shall remain valid forever, or should presume to dispossess or molest the Church of blessed Cyrus or its pastor in any way with respect to the possessions named above, let him pay one thousand pounds of the purest gold: one half to the holy Church of Ticinum and the other half to our treasury.

And so that this may be believed more truly and preserved inviolate by all, we have confirmed this decree with our hand and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

**Sign of the lord Henry, unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Henry, chancellor, acting in place of Everard, bishop and archchaplain, has examined and authenticated this document.

Made in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1013, indiction XII, in the thirteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done at Soleya.

---

### LXXXIII. Saint Henry the emperor grants certain estates situated outside the city of Bamberg to the abbey of Saint Michael. (Year 1015)

*[Ludewig, Scriptores rerum Germanicarum, 1118.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, the second, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

We wish the prudent knowledge of Christ’s faithful, both future and present, to know that by an imperial edict we decree that, among the estates which, out of regard for divine mercy, we have granted with imperial munificence to the Church of Saint Michael of Bamberg, together with our beloved wife Cunegund, for the salvation of our souls and of the souls of those to whom we are indebted, namely thirteen principal estates—Ratelsdorf, Ezelkirchen, Rodeheim, Belbenhusen, Werde, Wofurte, Dorffling, Ebelsfeld, Leitterbach, Elsendorff, and those around Wedereda, Scheistein, Husen, and Budensheim—with all the villages belonging to them, and also all estates acquired or to be acquired anywhere—the procurators of the said Church shall have free authority, at the pleasure of their abbot and superior, to place, establish, remove, and exchange for the better, as well as to administer manses, feudal holdings, plots, meadows, vineyards, woods, and other movable and immovable property.

We also wish all the Church’s tenants to render settlements for offenses, satisfactions or amends for transgressions or acts of violence, in every civil case, both at the three courts of May, autumn, and February and in all other business.

Furthermore, if the cultivators disagree among themselves when deciding legal disputes, we establish that they are to have recourse to the nearest court of the marquisate for judgment. If the case is complicated and difficult, they are to have recourse to the head of the monastery, that is, to the presence of the abbot.

The abbot shall then summon the leading and best men of his household and, with their counsel, order and arrange what is just.

The proper services of ploughing three times a year; eggs at Easter; cheeses at Pentecost; chickens at Carnival; and weekly services shall all be rendered to the said Church by everyone, as is fitting.

As for the final census, by which omitted or neglected services are in any event supplied—namely, the principal due—we decree that men shall send to the Church the best horse, or, if they lack a horse, the best head of livestock; and women shall send clothing and garments, so that together with the servants of the Church they may share fully in divine services.

So that the authority of this institution may remain stable and unshaken for all time and be observed inviolably by all, we have ordered this charter, written out for that purpose as appears below, to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Given on the Nones of February, indiction XII, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1015, in the sixteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, and in the fourth year of his empire.

Done successfully at Frankfurt. Amen.

---

### LXXXIV. Saint Henry confirms the possessions of the abbey of Saint Vanne. (Year 1015)

*[D. Calmet, Histoire de Lorraine, Preuves, p. 398.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the disposing clemency of God, Augustus, emperor.

It is renowned, and so forth. Therefore, let all the fellow-members of the palace and our other faithful know how, through the intervention of Heymo, our faithful servant and bishop of the holy Church of Verdun, we were asked to offer, by a decree of confirmation—as had been customary for the emperors and kings who preceded us—the possessions of his church formerly granted by an apostolic privilege and by a decree of our predecessor Otto of blessed memory to the church and monastery of blessed Peter.

There Berengarius, bishop of blessed memory, had adorned the rule of blessed Benedict the abbot, begun with sacred devotion, according to monastic ability, and had left it to be granted to his successors. We were also asked to offer what he had donated to that monastery and to strengthen it with our assent.

This was devoutly requested and granted by royal authority. Therefore, we give and transfer into the legal possession of the aforesaid Church the abbey itself, which is called Saint Vanne, together with everything belonging to it, and so forth.

The gift of Count Gerard to Saint Julian: one and a half manses and a vineyard, and so forth.

Our faithful Count Godfrey likewise gave certain possessions, listed below, to the aforesaid place in a village called Borbat: twenty manses with a church, and so forth.

The venerable Count Herman also granted to it thirty manses in the county of Brabant, on an estate called Haslud, and so forth.

Count Lutard, having become a monk in the same monastery, gave in the district of Vôge, in the county of Dagsburg, the estate of Balliodium—namely, a church with its endowment, a demesne manse, and forty others, and so forth.

For the salvation of our soul and of that of our most beloved wife Cunegund, and in commemoration of all our parents, to whose memories we acknowledge our obligation, we give to the aforesaid Church as its own one half of the toll, the mint, and the entire due belonging from that place to our jurisdiction, at a place called Mouzon.

Through the intervention of Count Herman, whose benefice it had previously been, we hand these things over and strengthen them by imperial authority, and so forth.

**Sign of the lord Henry, unconquered emperor Augustus.**

Gontherius, chancellor, acting in place of Herimbald, archchancellor, has examined and authenticated this document.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1015, in the fourteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, and in the second year of his empire.

Done at Neomagus.

---

### LXXXV. Confirmation of the rights and privileges of the convent of the sacred virgins of Lucca, Saint Saviour, made to Abbess Alperga by Saint Henry, first among the Augusti. (Year 1015)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, vol. I, 1007.]*

#### [Col. 0322A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Augustus, emperor of the Romans.

Whatever we bestow upon places dedicated to divine worship as a gift of our liberality, we do not doubt in the least that it will benefit us as a reward of eternal recompense. Let the discernment, therefore, of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own people, present and future, know how we, at the intervention and petition of the empress Cunegunda, our beloved [Col. 0322B] wife, by this page of our charter, insofar as we justly and legally can, confirm and strengthen the monastery of Saint Saviour, built within the walls of the city of Lucca, together with the abbess named Alperga, and with all the nuns serving God there, both those who are there now and those who in due course shall serve God there, together with all their possessions and properties—that is, lands, vineyards, meadows, pastures, woods, grazing grounds, and every substance which that place is entitled to possess. We confirm these things by the [charter] of our imperial power, by which that monastery, together with the property it already holds and that which still justly remains in the right of the monastery, may be maintained in the future.

We therefore establish, by this charter of our confirmation, that from now on and for the future the aforesaid [Col. 0322C] monastery, together with the property or dependants justly belonging to it, or whatever may hereafter have been bestowed upon it through the gift of religious men or devout women, shall remain under the confirmation of our charter; and that no one shall ever presume at any time to cause any disturbance concerning the aforesaid property, which they then appeared to hold peacefully and legally. Rather, by this authority of ours, all the property of that monastery shall be protected under the confirmation of our charter.

We also wish the aforesaid monastery, together with all property and dependants justly belonging to it, to exist under our immunity in our time and in that of our successors. And whenever the abbess dies, let them choose from among their own number as abbess the woman whom they find to be the best in good conduct. We also command and, by commanding, order that no public judge or anyone exercising judicial authority enter the monastery itself, or its churches, villages, or fields, etc.

That this may be believed all the more firmly, etc.

Sign of Lord Henry, most serene and most unconquered emperor Augustus.

Henry, chancellor, acting in place of Everard, bishop and archchancellor, has verified this.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the twelfth indiction, in the twelfth year of the reign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done in the county of Pisa, in the village called Fasiano, happily. Amen.

[Col. 0323A] A bull was hanging from it, which is now missing.

### LXXXVI. Saint Henry’s charter by which he restored to the Church of Saint Alexander of Bergamo the county of Alamannus, of which Count Atto had instituted that church as heir. (Year 1015.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IV, 439.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

If we grant anything that supplements the possessions of the churches of God, we do not doubt that merit will accrue to us from it. Therefore, we wish it to be known to the whole of the holy Church of God and to our faithful, present and future, that, kindled by love of God and of blessed Alexander [Col. 0323B] the martyr, through whose aid we believe that we shall prosper forever, we have suitably granted and strengthened for that church an imperial charter of our authority, insofar as we justly and legally can, just as formerly, as we believe, by royal investiture, the court of Lemen, together with all the castles belonging to it—namely Brivio and Lavello—was granted, just as Count Atto and his wife Ferlinda transferred it by a testamentary document to the bishopric of the aforesaid martyr Alexander: that is, with the lands belonging to it, vineyards, meadows, pastures, woods, mills, fisheries, waters and watercourses, and also male and female slaves, *aldi* and *aldianae*.

We therefore establish by this charter of our confirmation, just as the aforesaid count and his wife established, that from now on and in the future the bishopric of blessed Alexander the martyr, which is called Bergamo, shall have, hold, and firmly possess these things, with all opposition by every person removed. Accordingly, we command that no duke, margrave, count, archbishop, bishop, viscount, *gastald*, dean, or any great or small person of our empire dare molest or presume to disturb the aforesaid bishopric of blessed Alexander the martyr, or the bishop who is now in office, or those who shall be there in due course, without a legal judgment.

But if anyone should ever become a violator of this charter of ours—which we do not believe will happen—let him know that he shall pay one thousand pounds of the finest gold, half to our treasury and half to the aforesaid bishopric. That this may be believed more firmly and observed more carefully by everyone, we have strengthened it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the twelfth year of the reign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the first year of his empire.

Done in the county of Pisa, in the village called Fasiona, happily. Amen.

### LXXXVII. Saint Henry asserts to Bernard, count of Parma, possession of the court of Neroniana. (Year 1015.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, II, 161.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

Because of divine …, etc. Therefore, let it be known to the whole body of our faithful, present and future, that, recognizing in Otto, our lord and predecessor the emperor, the favour that promotes this recompense, we donate, grant, and bestow in full upon Bernard, count of Parma and our most faithful servant, through the intervention and petition of Cunegunda, empress Augustus, our wife, the court of Neiron, with its chapels, demesne castles, tenant-farms, villages, and lands, and everything belonging to it; also the court of Rocha and the castle in the valley of Visenerina, with everything belonging or adjoining to them, and whatever may be said or named, just as formerly Hugh, margrave of Tuscany, held all these things.

Since our lord, the emperor Otto, gave and granted to the aforesaid Count Bernard what we have mentioned, for his worthy service, and by his imperial right bestowed and granted it as property and dominion, we likewise, for the future from this time onward, give and confirm it by donation and grant, and strengthen it with perpetual stability in full, just as written above, together with male and female slaves, *aldiones*, *aldianae*, mountain lands, plains, mountains, hills, cliffs, pastures, woods, waters, fisheries, usages, watercourses, mills, and all the advantages of that court.

This is on the condition that from this hour onward the aforesaid Count Bernard shall have, hold, and firmly possess all the aforesaid property of that court by our donation, grant, and confirmation; and that by this page of our charter he and his heirs and heirs’ heirs, or anyone to whom he gives it or whom he appoints to hold it, shall have free power to hold, possess, give, exchange, or do with it whatever he decides [sic] should be done, with opposition or molestation by all persons in our kingdom and empire removed.

Therefore we command and order that no king, margrave, bishop, count, viscount, or any great or small person of our empire or kingdom presume to molest, disturb, or dispossess the aforesaid Count Bernard or his [Col. 0324D] heirs and heirs’ heirs concerning the aforesaid property of that court. If anyone, however, etc., becomes a violator of this donation of ours, let him know that he shall pay—

Sign of Lord Henry, most glorious and unconquered emperor Augustus.

Henry, bishop and chancellor, acting in place of Everard, bishop and archchancellor, has verified this.

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the fourteenth indiction, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the second year of his empire.

Done at Maresbuch, happily. Amen.

### LXXXVIII. Saint Henry gives the court of Honstede to the Church of Paderborn. Year 1015.

[*Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae*, p. 64.]

[Col. 0325A]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

When a good matter is undertaken, it is necessary first to overcome its … in the heart, lest, if it proceed from the root of a wretched intention, it produce the bitter fruits of wickedness. Therefore, as hearers not deaf to the evangelical Martha, after whose example Bishop Meinwerk strives to serve us through frequent ministry, at the intervention of Cunegunda, empress Augustus, namely our wife, and also of Everhard, [Col. 0325B] bishop of the holy see of Bamberg, and of Egilbert, bishop of the Church of Freising, we have transferred to the sacred church of Paderborn, consecrated in honour of Saint Mary, mistress of the world, and of Saint Kilian the martyr and Saint Liborius, confessor of the Lord, the court called Honstede, with all its appurtenances—namely cultivated and uncultivated lands, male and female dependants, mills, fisheries, waters and watercourses—which Archbishop Unwan possessed and legally transferred to us—in the district of Rittiga, in the county of Count Bernhard—to be possessed in perpetuity.

And so that this authority of our imperial transfer may remain firm and unshaken, we have strengthened this document with our own hand and ordered it to be authenticated by the impression of our seal.

[Col. 0325C] Sign of Lord Henry (L. M.), most unconquered emperor.

I, Gunterius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain, have recorded this.

Given on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the thirteenth indiction, and in the thirteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the first year of his empire.

Done at Mulinhusen, happily. Amen.

### LXXXIX. Exchange of property between the emperor Henry II and Abbot Bobbo. (Year 1015, 11 May.)

[Dronke, *Codex diplomaticus Fuldensis*, p. 346.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor [Col. 0325D] Augustus of the Romans.
