Let it be known to the whole body of all our faithful, present and future, how it pleased us to make an exchange with Bobbo, abbot of Fulda, with the consent and approval of his advocate Bernhard, and also of his monks, knights, and servants. We received from him as our property two courts, Ratolfesdorf and Ezelenkyricha, with all their appurtenances: villages, male and female dependants, fields, open country, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, roads and trackless places, exits and entrances, cultivated and uncultivated lands, things acquired or to be acquired, and every advantage that can in any way be said or named [Col. 0326A].

In return, to the aforesaid abbot and to his abbey, built in honour of Saint Boniface, we grant and bestow by this imperial page two courts belonging to us, one called Waraha and the other Bereskyez, with all their appurtenances, together with four of my ministeriales: Alwino and Rodolfo, my stewards, and Folcold and Erkenger, my marshals; as well as the remaining male and female dependants, fields, open country, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, roads and trackless places, exits and entrances, cultivated and uncultivated lands, things acquired or to be acquired, and every advantage that can in any way be said or named. Through this imperial page we grant and bestow them as property and transfer them completely from our right and dominion into his right and dominion.

This is on the condition that the aforesaid Abbot Bobbo and his successors shall thereafter have free power, for the benefit of the aforesaid church, to do whatever they please with the courts just mentioned and their appurtenances, with opposition by all persons removed. And so that this authority of our exchange or donation may remain stable and unshaken for all time, we have strengthened this imperial charter, drawn up for this purpose, with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Henry, most serene (M) and unconquered emperor Augustus (S).

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the fifth day before the Ides of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0326C] 1015, in the twelfth indiction, in the thirteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the second year of his empire.

Done at Chofunga, happily. Amen.

### XC. The emperor Henry gives to the Church of Bamberg two places, Schwarzenfeld and Weilendorf, in the district of Nordgau. (Year 1015, 17 April.)

[Ried, *Codex episcopatus Ratisbonensis*, I, 132.]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

If we strive to enrich or improve venerable places of the Churches of God by some gift, we do not doubt that this will greatly benefit us and the stability of our kingdom. [Col. 0326D] Therefore, let the whole body of Christ’s faithful and of our own people know how we, for the salvation of our soul and those of our parents, with the intervention and petition of Eberhard, venerable prelate of that Church, grant and bestow upon the Church of Bamberg—which we raised from our inheritance and advanced as an episcopal see under the patronage of blessed Mary, Mother of God, and Saint Peter, prince of the apostles—certain places belonging to us, named Schwarzenfeld and Weilendorf, in the district of Nordgau and in the county of Count Henry, with all their appurtenances: cultivated and uncultivated lands, male and female dependants, buildings, sites, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, pastures, meadows, exits and [Col. 0327A] entrances, things acquired and to be acquired, and all other advantages that can in any way be named and that belong to Schwarzenfeld. Through this imperial page we transfer them from our right and dominion into its right and dominion.

This is on the condition that the same Bishop Eberhard and his successors shall thereafter have free power to do whatever they wish with them for the use of the Church of Bamberg, with opposition by all persons in our kingdom removed. And so that this authority of our transfer may remain stable and unshaken through future generations, we have strengthened this charter of ours with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

[Col. 0327B] Sign of Lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus of the Romans. (Monogram.)

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the fourteenth indiction, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the second year of his empire.

Done at Merseburg, happily.

With the seal of majesty.

### XCI. Saint Henry bestows upon Alberic, bishop of Como, the court or village of the Branzanorum, formerly belonging to Berengar and Hugh, sons of Count Sigifred, rebels against the imperial majesty. (Year 1015.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, V, 282.]

[Col. 0327C]

In the name of the Lord God and our Saviour Jesus Christ, Henry, by heavenly clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

If we incline the ears of our piety to the petitions of our faithful who duly serve us, we do not doubt that they will become more ready in our service. Therefore, we wish it by no means to remain unknown to the whole body of those obedient to us, present and future, that Alberic, venerable bishop of the Holy Church of Como and our beloved servant, humbly approached the loftiness of our piety, asking that, for the love of the eternal Rewarder, for the salvation of our soul, in return for his service already rendered and to be rendered, and for the advancement of our empire, we might grant and give to that holy mother church, dedicated to the honour [Col. 0327D] of God’s Mother and Virgin Mary, a certain court with all its appurtenances, called the village of the Branzanorum, which had been the inheritance and property of the sons of Count Sigifred, Berengar and Hugh.

Because they had offended us excessively, treated our empire wickedly, and had publicly become perjurers and guilty rebels against our majesty, by right and legally not only these possessions but everything they had came into our public domain. Therefore they deservedly lose all that was theirs, since they freely destroyed themselves: forgetting the faith owed to us, they did not remain in our allegiance but swore allegiance to and joined our enemy.

Seeing this petition as worthy and valid, [Col. 0328A] and unwilling in any way to deny his requests, we willingly consented to them. We grant and confirm to the same venerable and beloved bishop of Como and to all his successors the aforesaid court called Branzanorum, with all its appendages, all its revenues, renderings, outlays, and dues, with male and female slaves, *aldii* and *aldiae*, both in the mountains and on the plain, cultivated and uncultivated lands, vineyards, fields, pastures, woods, tenant-farms, tenant holdings, waters, watercourses, mills, houses, all movable and immovable property, and everything else that may still be said or named as belonging to the same court.

We grant it entirely and transfer and assign it from our right, dominion, and ownership into the right, dominion, and ownership [Col. 0328B] of the aforesaid holy church. Thus the bishop who is now in office and all his successors shall have the power to hold, possess, and exchange the aforesaid court, with everything belonging to it, just as these things had appeared until now to belong to the aforesaid perjurers and as they had possessed their inheritances. And the same bishops shall have full authority from us to do with that court and with everything that can thereafter be rendered whatever they please, to the praise and honour of God and Saint Mary.

Therefore, by our command, we decree that in our time or in that of our successors no duke, margrave, count, viscount, or any great or small person, of whatever rank or order, presume to dispossess, disturb, molest, or in any way diminish the aforesaid Bishop Alberic or his successors concerning the aforesaid court and all its appurtenances. Rather, let them be permitted to hold, possess, and firmly retain it peacefully and quietly, with all opposition removed.

But if anyone—which we hardly believe—becomes a violator of the provisions of this charter of ours, let him know with certainty that he shall pay one thousand pounds of gold, one part to our treasury and the other to the aforesaid bishop and his successors. And so that this may be believed more firmly and observed by all as stable and unshaken, we have confirmed it with our own hand, with the character of our name inscribed, and with the impression of our seal …

Sign of Lord Henry +, most glorious emperor, forever Augustus.

Henry, bishop of Parma and chancellor, [Col. 0328D] acting in place of Everard, bishop and archchancellor, has verified this.

Given on the fourth day before the Nones of October, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1015, in the fourteenth indiction, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus, and in the second year of his empire.

Done at Merseburg, happily. Amen.

### XCII. Saint Henry gives certain estates to the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1016.)

[*Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae*, p. 7.]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God, emperor of the Romans.

If we devote ourselves with every effort to the advancement of the Churches of God, we hope that the rewards of eternal recompense will come to us. Therefore, let the whole body of Christ’s faithful, present and future, know how Meinwerk, venerable bishop of the holy Church of Paderborn, transferred to his mother, Adela, all the estates that he had possessed by hereditary right. Thereafter she, with the hand of her husband and advocate, Count Balderic, and with the consent of the heirs, donated those same estates to us with full authority.

We, however, admonished by hope of everlasting blessedness and by the pious prayer and devotion of the aforesaid bishop and our beloved nephew, who rejoices to dedicate himself and all that is his to divine service, bestow upon the holy Church of Paderborn, constructed in honour of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of Saint Kilian the martyr and blessed Liborius the confessor, the same estates, legally transferred to us. Among them are chiefly these courts: Immideshusun, Walmonthem, Havurlon, Hukilhem, [Col. 0329B] Mandelbiki, Golthbiki, Doddonhusun, Hokinneslevo, and Wakereslevo, with the villages belonging to them, male and female dependants, woods, roads and trackless places, exits and entrances, mills, fisheries, pastures, hunting rights, things acquired and to be acquired, and all utensils that can in any way be said or named. We grant them with opposition by all persons removed.

Moreover, by imperial authority we command that no person, great or small, exercising any judicial power, intrude upon these estates, except the advocate whom the bishop of that church chooses for himself. But if anyone, which God forbid, should dare to violate this charter of our donation, let him pay one hundred pounds of gold, fifty to that church and fifty to our treasury. And so that this authority of our gift may remain firm and unshaken, we have strengthened this charter, drawn up for that purpose, with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Henry, unconquered emperor of the Romans (L. M.).

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchambald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1016, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the second year of his empire.

Done at Drodmannia, happily. Amen.

### XCIII. Saint Henry bestows the court of Moronga upon the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1016.)

[*Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae*, p. 72.]

[Col. 0329D]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

The imperial order requires us to enlarge the Churches of Christ and to provide piously and mercifully for the needs of his servants. Therefore, let the discernment of Christ’s faithful know how, warned by divine inspiration, and through the intervention of our beloved wife, Cunigunda, empress Augustus, with Heribert, archbishop of Cologne, Theoderic of Minden, Adalbold of Utrecht, Theoderic of Metz, Wigger of Verden, Thietmar of Osnabrück, and Eric of Havelberg cooperating in the same matter through fraternal charity, we grant and bestow through this imperial page upon the holy Church of Paderborn, constructed in honour of holy Mary, Mother of God, Saint Kilian the martyr, and Saint Liborius the confessor, over which the venerable Bishop Meinwerk presides, a certain court of ours called Moronga, situated in the district of Moronga, in the county of Count Benno.

Unwan, archbishop of Bremen, transferred it to us with the hand of his advocate Udo. We grant it with opposition by all persons removed, for the salvation of the soul of our lord, the emperor Augustus Otto III, of divine memory, and for the preservation of our present life and the hope of the future, together with all its appurtenances: sites, villages, pastures, waters and watercourses, fisheries, mills, woods, hunting rights, and all utensils that may in any way be named.

This is on the condition that the aforesaid Bishop Meinwerk shall possess the same court with full authority for his own use as long as he lives; but after the end of his life it shall belong to the annually improved clothing allowance of the canons serving God and his holy Mother Mary, as well as the blessed Kilian and Liborius, in that place. If anyone should presume to violate this donation of ours, let him pay one hundred pounds of gold, fifty to that church and fifty to our treasury. And so that this authority of our liberality may remain stable and unshaken, we have strengthened this charter, drawn up for that purpose, with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Lord Henry, unconquered emperor.

(L. M.)

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1016, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the second year of his empire.

Done at Drodmannia, happily. Amen.

### XCIV. Likewise the court of Berneshusen. (In the same year.)

[The same source.]

[Col. 0330D] In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

We enlarge the tribunal of the soul when we enlarge the Churches of Christ together with those subject to them. Therefore, let it be known to the whole body of God’s faithful that with this intention, through the intervention of our beloved wife, Cunigunda, empress Augustus, and also of Heribert, archbishop of Cologne; Adalbold of Utrecht; Theoderic of Minden; Theoderic of Metz; Wigger of Verden; Thietmar of Osnabrück; and Eric of Havelberg, we grant by proprietary right to the holy Church of Paderborn, consecrated in honour of holy Mary, Mother of God, Saint Kilian the martyr, and Saint Liborius, over which the venerable Bishop Meinwerk presides, a certain court belonging to us called Berneshusen, situated in the district of Lisgau, in the county of Udo.

We received it as a lawful transfer from Unwan, archbishop of Bremen, who donated it through his advocate Udo. We grant it for the salvation of the soul of the emperor Otto III, of divine memory, namely our lord, and for the preservation of the present and future life of both ourselves and our most beloved wife, and no less for the stability of the kingdom, together with all its appurtenances: territorial property, villages, male and female dependants, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, roads and trackless places, exits and entrances, meadows and pastures, and everything acquired or to be acquired.

This is on the condition that the aforesaid bishop and his [Col. 0331B] successors shall have free power to convert it to the benefit of that church. But if anyone in the future—which God forbid—attempts to disturb the aforesaid church concerning these estates, let him be condemned by perpetual anathema. Moreover, let him pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold, half to the royal treasury and the other half to the same church which he presumed to disturb. And so that this authority of our transfer may remain stable and unshaken, we have strengthened this charter, drawn up for that purpose, with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus (L. M.).

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erchenbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0331C] 1016, in the fourteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, but in the second year of his empire. Done at Drodmannia.

### XCV. Likewise the possessions of the deceased Count Hahold. (In the same year.)

[The same source, p. 73.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

The clemency of divine compassion, which raised us to the summit of imperial majesty, willed us to reign for this purpose: that we might assist in strengthening and consolidating the order of the Churches, especially those places founded by our predecessors, kings or emperors, but which, because of the demands of sin, appeared already almost destroyed. [Col. 0331D]

Therefore, we wish it to be known to the discernment of all our faithful, present and future, how we, moved by divine love, for the salvation of our soul and those of our parents, as well as of the emperor Otto III, of good memory, through the intervention of our beloved wife Cunigunda, empress Augustus, and at the request of Meinwerk, venerable bishop of the holy Church of Paderborn, grant and bestow as property upon him and his holy church—formerly founded by the emperor Charles the Great but in our time afflicted by fire, and dedicated in honour of holy Mary, Mother of God and ever-virgin, and of Saint Kilian the martyr and Liborius the confessor—the county that Count Hahold held during his lifetime, situated in the following places: Haverga, Limga, Thiatmalli, Aga, Patherga, Treveresga, Langaneka, Erpesfeld, Silbike, Matfelt, Nihterga, Sinatfelt, Ballevan near Spriada, Bambiki, Gession, and Seuvardeshuson, with all its legal rights.

This is on the condition that the aforesaid Bishop Meinwerk and his successors, presiding over the aforesaid church, shall thereafter have free power to do with that county and its advantages whatever they please, for their benefit and that of the church, with every disturbance removed. And so that this authority of our transfer and confirmation may be held stable and unshaken for all time, we have taken care to strengthen this charter, drawn up for that purpose, with our own hand [Col. 0332B] and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Lord Henry, emperor Augustus (L. M.).

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Erkinbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1016, in the thirteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, and in the second year of his empire.

### XCVI. Likewise certain estates. (In the same year.

[The same source, p. 74.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

Let the discernment of all Christ’s faithful know how [Col. 0332C] we, out of regard for divine love and at the request and prompting of our most beloved wife, Cunigunda, empress Augustus—we two being one flesh—made over as property to the holy Church of Paderborn, dedicated in honour of holy Mary, Mother of God, Saint Kilian the martyr, and Saint Liborius, thrice-blessed confessor, an estate such as Helmic transferred to us, with opposition by all persons removed, namely in the county of Count Hermann:

in Dulmine, one holding; in Nienhem, one holding; in Situnne, one holding; in Halostron, one holding; in Berthalostron, one holding; in Lehembeke, one holding; and in Horlon, one holding;

and in the county of Count Otto:

in Elvepo, one holding; and in Ricoldinchuson, one holding;

together with fifty male and female dependants, sites, villages, pastures, [Col. 0332D] waters and watercourses, fisheries, mills, woods, hunting rights, all appendages, and every utensil that may in any way be named.

This is on the condition that each of us, both in clothing and in food, shall henceforth receive and possess there, as one of the brothers, a full stipend from the bishop of the aforesaid see—now from Lord Bishop Meinwerk and thereafter from his successors—with the common consent of the canons and with perpetual participation in their prayers.

And so that this transfer of our liberality may remain stable and unshaken, we have strengthened this charter, drawn up for that purpose, with our own hand and ordered it to be sealed below with our seal.

[Col. 0333A] Sign of Lord Henry, unconquered emperor Augustus of the Romans (L. M.).

I, Guntherius, chancellor, acting in place of Archanbald, archchaplain, have verified this.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of June, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1017, in the sixteenth year of the reign of Lord Henry II, and in the fourth year of his empire. Done at Paderborn.

### XCVII. Saint Emperor Henry II provides for the immunity of the Church of Trier to Poppo. (Year 1016.)

[Hontheim, *Historia Trevirensis diplomatica*, I, 351.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity [Note: [Col. 0333D] Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, king. I assign this charter, lacking a date, to the first year of Poppo because in that year the emperor was at Trier. Thus the *Acts of Trier*, chapter 48: “After Bishop Megingaud of the metropolitan see of Trier had been removed from this life, the king himself hastened to Trier; for he was staying at Confluentia; and, having obtained the consent of both clergy and people, he elevated him to the pontifical see.” It is remarkable, however, that Henry, already crowned emperor in the year 1014, calls himself king. This is admitted by the bishop of Gottwic in the *Chronicon*, preliminary volume, p. 233. Compare what will be said concerning the bull of Pope Benedict VIII in the following year.] Henry, by the favour of divine clemency, king.

[Col. 0333B] If we bestow some benefit upon places dedicated to God, in accordance with the petitions of God’s servants and through the gift of our liberality, we plainly believe that this will profit us both for passing through mortal life in time and for attaining eternal life happily.

Therefore we wish it to be made known to our faithful, both present and future, that the venerable Poppo, archbishop of the holy Church of Trier, has often admonished us and petitioned our sublimity that we might deign to recall and confirm under our scepters, for the strengthening thereof, the abundance of goods and dependents of Saint Peter which our predecessors—namely, kings and emperors—assigned to the see of Trier out of regard for divine contemplation and confirmed by the authority of their commands.

Gladly consenting to his petition, and decreeing that this command of our authority toward that Church be made out of fear and love of God, we firmly order and establish that, over the estates or properties belonging to the Church of Saint Peter of the city of Trier—namely, monasteries, basilicas, castles, villages, fields, vineyards, forests, people, or other possessions, and everything which divine clemency may henceforth wish to increase in the right of that place—no count or anyone exercising judicial power may dare, in our time or in the future, to intervene for hearing cases, exacting fines, taxes, or any other levies, requiring lodgings or provisions, distraining the men of the Church, demanding unjust exactions, or collecting tolls; nor may anyone presume to exact in full any of the things mentioned above.

Rather, let everything remain under the right of Saint Peter, of the see of Trier, and of its bishop, and of whoever he himself entrusts with it. Let him also lawfully possess in perpetuity the mints and tolls which the aforementioned bishop found in the endowment of his Church or subsequently acquired from our predecessors.

Moreover, in accordance with the commands of our ancestors, and entirely for the sake of alms for ourselves and our parents, we strictly forbid that a toll be collected in the village of Theodon from the goods of the brothers serving the prince of the apostles at Trier, or from their men, whether they reside there or in the village of Madert; this provision being that they may keep watch in prayer on our behalf.

This, and whatever else we have approved concerning the aforesaid property of the Church, we have confirmed by the authority of our scepter. So that this may be believed by men in the present and future, and more diligently observed by our successors, we have confirmed it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry III, most invincible king.

XCVIII. Charter of Saint Henry II, emperor, granted to Werenher, bishop of Strasbourg. (Year 1017.)

[Gallia Christiana V, 469, Documents]

[Col. 0334B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God Augustus of the Romans.

Let it be known to all the faithful of Christ that, through the intervention of our beloved wife Cunigunda, namely the empress Augusta, and also of Bruno, bishop of Augsburg, our brother, as well as of Poppo, venerable abbot of Lorsch, we have, for the special love of the Mother of God Mary and also on account of the continual service, both spiritual and material, which he has most generously and frequently rendered to us, defined and granted to Werenher, venerable bishop of the holy see of Strasbourg, the forest:

from the bank of the Rhine opposite Witzwilare to Hugo’s ford; from Hugo’s ford to Seerovillare; from Seerovillare to Dabechneinsten; [Col. 0334C] from Dabechneinsten beyond the Prusca as far as the Roraha stream; from the Roraha beyond the River Sorma; then as far as the River Meuse, to the place called Phaffenhovend; thereafter downstream along the Meuse to where the Meuse enters the Rhine; and then upstream along the entire boundary of the Rhine, with all the adjacent islands, as far as Wicenwilare.

Therefore we have confirmed to him and to his successors the right of the forest, according to the custom of our royal and imperial predecessors, by our imperial ban. Thus no one may in any way capture there, without his permission, a stag or hind, bear, boar, or [lacuna] he-goats or she-goats.

And so that this authority of our donation may remain firm and unshaken for all time, we have signed this document written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal. [Col. 0334D]

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible.

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain.

Given on the seventh day before the Ides of May, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1017, indiction 15, and in the sixteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, the fourth of his empire. Done happily at Frankfurt.

XCVIII bis. Saint Henry grants the abbey of Helmwardeshusen to the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1017.)

[Codex Diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae, p. 74.]

[Col. 0335A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God Roman emperor Augustus.

The statutes of the canons, established not by human speech but by the Spirit of God, command that bishops frequently visit the cloisters of monks and, if they find anything there outside the rule, cut it away and correct it. Contemplating these things attentively within ourselves, and lightening our burdens on the journey of this life by laying them upon bishops, for the sake of charity, without which the rich person is poor, with the intervention of our most beloved wife Cunigunda, [Col. 0335B] namely the empress Augusta, and with that of the archbishops Erchanbald of Mainz, Poppo of Trier, Gero of Magdeburg, and Unwan of Bremen, and of the bishops Arnold of Halberstadt, Eppo of Bamberg, Theoderic of Metz, Henry of Würzburg, Theoderic of Münster, Henry of Parma, Theoderic of Minden, Thietmar of Merseburg, and Eric of Havelberg, and also of the laymen Duke Bernhard and Counts Sigifrid and Ezzico, we have given to the see of Paderborn—built in honor of holy Mary and Saints Kilian and Liborius, over which the distinguished prelate Meinwerk, its notable acquisition, presently presides—the abbey called Helmwardeshusen, with all its movable and immovable appurtenances, as its own property.

We have transferred it from our right and dominion into the right and dominion of that see, to be henceforth administered and possessed episcopally, with full authority and in accordance with the rule of Saint Benedict. And so that this document of our transfer may remain firm and unshaken, we have strengthened and confirmed it with our own hand and ordered it to be sealed below with the impression of our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus (L. M.).

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain.

Given on the fifth day before the Ides of July, indiction 12, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1017, and in the sixteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, the fourth of his empire. Done at Lietzo.

These are the witnesses: Thietmer, Ekkica, Ludier, Ekkica, [Col. 0335D] Raedig, Walhem, Widukin, Benna, Kiza, Amulag, Volcbal, Thietmer, Immed, Gerbraht, Wiking, Thiedric, Ibo, Aeica, Heriward, Burchard, Dodica, Tiaza, Vretheric, Lefherd, Eschulf, Ova, Widula, Fronca, Heriman, Thiaza, Bova.

Bishop Theoderic.

Duke Bernhard.

Concerning the abbey of Helmuwrdesh.

XCIX. Diploma of Saint Henry for the abbey of Saint Peter of Piro. (Year 1017.)

[Ughelli, *Italia Sacra*, X, 207.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, [Col. 0336A] Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

If we strive to improve the places of God’s Churches or of monks by the gift of some confirmation or protection, we have no doubt that this will be of benefit to us. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of Christ, present and future, how we, moved by divine love, offer and donate to the aforesaid [lacuna] abbey, [lacuna] from our predecessors [lacuna] and situated in the place called Pirus, in the county of Treviso, dedicated in honor of Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, with all its dependencies which once belonged to it through the donation of our predecessors and which the aforesaid abbey presently possesses, [Col. 0336B] for the remedy of our sins, [lacuna], and also at the request of our beloved and faithful John, [lacuna], patriarch of Aquileia, [lacuna], the village of Saint Paul with its dependencies and the chapel of Saint Marinus with its appurtenances—namely, manses, houses, lands, vineyards, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, fisheries, mills, roads and trackless ways, [lacuna], exits and revenues, those acquired or to be acquired, or all utilities which can in any manner be said or named—by this our command we confirm and strengthen them.

Moreover, we receive the aforesaid abbey, together with its abbot, named Adalbert, and his successors, under the protection and defense of our guardianship, [Col. 0336C] together with all the aforesaid equipment and goods, on the following condition: no duke, count, viscount, or any great or small person of our kingdom, whether ecclesiastical or secular authority, may dare henceforth to deprive the aforesaid monastery or abbot of the goods written above, disturb or harass them, or remove them from them without a lawful or imperial judgment.

If anyone, which God forbid, should prove to be a violator of this command of our confirmation and strengthening, or of our protective guardianship, let him know that he must pay one hundred pounds of the finest gold, half to our treasury and half to the aforesaid monastery and its abbots.

And so that the authority of this confirmation or protection may remain firm and unshaken forever, we have strengthened this document written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked below with our seal. [Col. 0336D]

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible and serene emperor Augustus.

I, John, now patriarch of the Church of Aquileia, approve and confirm.

I, Peregrinus, chancellor of the sacred palace, approve and confirm.

I, [lacuna]brandus, bishop and archchancellor of the most invincible emperor, approve and confirm.

In the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1017, indiction 1, in the fourteenth year of the lord Henry, king, and the fourth year of his empire, [lacuna] happily. Amen.

XCIX bis. Foundation of the collegiate church of Prüm, confirmed by the authority of Emperor Henry II. (Year 1017, 17 October.)

[Hontheim, *History of the Diplomas of Trier*, I, 253.]

[Col. 0337A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God emperor of the Romans.

We wish it to be known to all bishops, abbots, counts, and our other faithful, present and future, that Viroldus, abbot of Prüm, [Note: [Col. 0337C] Viroldus, abbot of Prüm. He was the seventeenth in number. Concerning him Knauff, *Defensio Prumiensis*, III, p. 44, says: “Abbot Uroldus, from the ancient line of counts of Duna, founded here at Prüm, with the community, a college of twelve canons as the perpetual chaplains of the abbot and community. He enriched the magnificently built and endowed church with the body of Saint Nazarius, in which he was buried and is commemorated annually. Add Mabillon, *Annales Benedictini*, vol. IV, book LIV, no. 42.] our faithful, constructing a certain monastery from its foundations with our permission and consent, and causing it to be dedicated in honor of Saint Salvator, our Lord Jesus Christ, of holy Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, of the most victorious cross, of Saint Stephen the protomartyr, [Col. 0337B] and of the illustrious martyr Saint Nazarius, commended it for defense under our imperial protection.

The aforesaid venerable abbot also explained to us that, with God’s assent and with our gracious consent, he wished to establish canons in the aforesaid monastery and to provide them, from properties which he had acquired by precarious tenure, [Note: [Col. 0337D] From properties which he himself acquired by precarious tenure. His successor Albero increased Uroldus’s prebend for the college. But after the revenues and number of clergy had been diminished by the storms of war, finally, around the year 1360, through the work of Archbishop Bohemund II and Abbot Theoderic, and by the concession of Pope Innocent III, the college’s possessions were restored, although the provostship was abolished. The abbot or administrator of Prüm confers all canonries and invests the elected dean.] without any loss to the monks subject to him, with a prebend. Their names are these: Wittenbach, Stadtfeld, Ludtscheim.

Granting his petition, and that of our other faithful who joined their prayers to his—namely Poppo, archbishop of Trier; Heribert of Cologne; Areckenbod of Mainz; Eberhard of Bamberg; Bruno of Augsburg; [Col. 0337C] Hehelin of Württemberg; Burchard of Worms; and the counts Gerlach, Gebhard, Bebenhard, and Brunung; as well as the abbots Poppo of Fulda, Winnerich of Trier, Luthard of Münchaurach, and Richard of Amelbach—we have received the aforesaid places under the immunity of our protection.

We have likewise lawfully established for the support of the brothers there a public market with all its rights, and an annual and weekly market. Through this imperial charter we order [Col. 0338A] and command that no one appropriate for himself anything from the aforesaid property that has been assigned to the brothers mentioned above, so that they may possess peacefully and quietly what God has given or will give, and may gladly implore God’s mercy for our safety and the stability of our kingdom.

And so that this authority of our command and donation may be more truly believed and more diligently observed by all, we ordered this charter to be written, confirmed by the subscription of our own hand, and marked with our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry, emperor of the Romans.

Gunther, later archbishop of Salzburg, chancellor and vice-archchancellor, Ludu archchancellor.

[Note: [Col. 0337D] Ludu, archchancellor. I leave to others the investigation of who this archchancellor may be, since he has not appeared in any diploma published thus far.]

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of November, indiction 15, in the year of the Lord’s [Col. 0338B] incarnation 1017, while the lord Henry II was reigning [sic] in his fifteenth year and in the third year of his empire.

Done happily at Frankfurt. Amen.

C. Saint Henry II, emperor, grants to Poppo and the Church of Trier the estate of Confluentia with all its dependencies. (Year 1018.)

[Hontheim, *History of the Diplomas of Trier*, I, 354.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

If we strive to exalt venerable places of God’s Churches by the advantage of some gift, we have no doubt that this will benefit us and the condition of our kingdom. [Col. 0338C] Therefore let the whole company of all our faithful and of the faithful of Christ know how we, for the remedy of our soul and also of that of our most beloved wife Cunigunda, namely the empress Augusta, have transferred and firmly donated to the Church of Trier, over which the venerable archbishop Poppo appears to preside, a certain estate belonging to our right, called Confluentia, and an abbey situated in the district of Trier, [Note: [Col. 0338D] An abbey situated in the district of Trier. Brower, *Annals*, vol. I, book XI, no. 16, p. 507, understands this less correctly as the abbey of Saint Servatius at Maastricht. For the emperor does not call it the abbey of Trier, but an abbey situated in the district of Trier, in which district Confluentia must be sought together with the abbey itself. This district occupies all the tract of land lying between the Hunsrück, the Rhine, and the Moselle, as far as the mouth of that river. But, you ask, what abbey was within Confluentia? I answer: the church and college of Saint Florian, which, as Brower himself testifies in the passage cited, p. 504, no. 4, was then called the monastery of the Blessed Virgin Mary, since in that age the term *monasterium* was nearly common to cathedral and collegiate churches. For canons formerly living in common were governed by abbots, though secular ones; on whose office and prerogatives see Molanus, *On Canons*, book II, chapter 5. Miraeus, *Belgian Diplomas*, book II, chapter 19, note 1, likewise relates that, in the usage and style of that age, colleges of canons were called abbeys among the people of Liège and others.] in the county of Count Berthold, with its toll and mint, and with all their dependencies. [Note: [Col. 0337D] An estate belonging to our right, called Confluentia. Royal estates and estates of the royal fisc were the places from which such revenues were drawn. Hence, in several diplomas, various revenues belonging to one royal estate or village are listed. At times, however, royal estates also designate the ruler’s palace. In both senses Confluentia was a royal estate.] in the county of Count Berthold, with its toll and mint, and with all their dependencies. [Note: [Col. 0338D] With its toll and mint and with all their dependencies, etc. It was finally by these words of the imperial command that Confluentia was subjected to the archbishop. Yet even now not in such a way that all authority of imperial officials ceased there. Compare the instrument of the foundation of Arnstein, year 1, 56, note a. It is indeed read in the *Deeds of Trier*, chapter 46, Leibniz edition, that Henry II confirmed to Megingaud, Poppo’s predecessor, the bishopric of Trier, which Megingaud administered until the end of his life in the castle of Confluentia. Likewise Alberic, under the year 1003, part II of the *Chronicle*, p. 42: “There was a long-lasting dissension, and Megingaud always remained at Confluentia.” More explicitly Thietmar, *Chronicle*, book VII, p. 406: “Megingaud died in his own city called Confluentia.” Hence, following Brower, *Annals of Trier*, vol. I, book X, no. 100, p. 502, Hahn concludes, *History of the Empire*, part II, chapter 6, § 6, note e, that Confluentia had already belonged to Trier before the year 1018. But a single passage of Thietmar can scarcely establish this. For if we understand the phrase “his own Confluentia” also in the civil sense, it is easy to suppose that the bishop of Merseburg used prolepsis in his *Chronicle*, which he wrote later and brought down to the year 1021. In any case, it is established that Megingaud did not withdraw voluntarily to Confluentia but was driven there by the violence of Provost Adalbero. See the *Deeds of Trier*, cited above; the *Life of Blessed Meinwerk*, § 10, in the Antwerp *Acta Sanctorum*, June, vol. I, p. 534, letter a; Alberic, cited above; the Saxon Chronicler under the year 1008, p. 220; Thietmar, p. 384.]

with lands, buildings, male and female slaves, fields, pastures, vineyards, meadows, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, mills, roads and trackless ways, revenues and proceeds, movable and immovable property, and every utility that could in any way be written or recorded. [Col. 0339A] And so that this document of our authority may remain firm and unshaken for all time, we have strengthened it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus.

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erchenbald, archchaplain.

In the year of the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ 1018, indiction 1, in the seventeenth year of the reign of the lord Henry, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus, and in the fifth year of his empire. Done happily at Boderebrunnen. Amen.

CI. Saint Henry grants a certain estate to the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1018.)

[Codex Diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae, p. 75.]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Let the diligence of all the faithful of God and of our own people, both present and future, know how we, through the intervention of our beloved wife Cunigunda, namely the empress Augusta, and of our faithful Poppo, archbishop of Trier; Erkanbald, [Col. 0339C] archbishop of Mainz; Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg; Adelbald, bishop of Utrecht; and likewise Poppo, abbot of Fulda; and through the intervention of Dukes Godefrid and Bernhard and Count Becelin, have given in perpetual ownership to the Church of Paderborn—built and dedicated in honor of the holy Mother of God Mary and of Saint Kilian the martyr, as well as of the most blessed confessor Saint Liborius the bishop, over which the venerable bishop Meinwerk presides, [Col. 0340A] being most ready for our service—a certain estate of the kind that Willa gave into our hand with the consent of her husband and advocate Otto, in the place called Siburgohusun, in the county of Count Udo, in the district of Hemmerveldun, with all its dependencies, possessions, male and female slaves, fields, buildings, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and watercourses, meadows, pastures and common pastures, mills, fisheries, woods, roads and trackless ways, and all things acquired or to be acquired.

And so that this transfer of our charter may remain firm and unshaken, we have strengthened this document written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be sealed below with the impression of our seal. [Col. 0340B]

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus (L. M.).

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erkanbald, archchaplain.

Given on the first day before the Ides of April, indiction 1, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1018, and in the sixteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, the fifth of his empire. Done at Nijmegen.

CII. Saint Henry, emperor, founds and endows the college of canons of Saint Adelbert at Aachen. [Note: [Col. 0339D]

At Aachen there are two colleges of canons, the Marian and the Adelbertine. The former was founded by the emperor Charlemagne, who wished it to reside in the round basilica which he had built there in his palace in honor of the Mother of God. He later increased its endowment. Otto, the first Caesar, also increased the number of canons, as did Notger, bishop of Liège, in whose diocese Aachen lies.

Moreover, the palace at Aachen was burned and devastated by Kings Godefrid and Sigefrid in the year 882, as Sigebert testifies in his *Chronicle*. But the chapel or basilica, constructed from its foundations by Charlemagne with extremely solid colonnades, still survives today in its round form, with marble columns, a vaulted roof, bronze screens and doors, and other ornaments which Einhard describes in the *Life of that same prince and master*, as we ourselves once observed while looking upon them with admiration.

The foundations of the Adelbertine church, once outside but now within the walls of Aachen and situated on a height, were laid at his own expense by the emperor Otto III, whose tomb is seen in the aforementioned Marian basilica. Saint Henry completed the building and endowed the canons with extensive estates, many of which, on the borders of Brabant and Zeeland, three miles from Antwerp near Batzentoren, were swallowed up and destroyed by the waters, together with the tower itself. The tower, standing amid the waters not far from Lillo, rose like a watchtower, but, eroded by the sea waves, collapsed a few years ago. Yet, I hope, the time will come when posterity, by means of alluvial deposits, will reclaim from the waves of the Ocean that once extensive tract of land for the benefit of the people of Aachen, Antwerp, and others.

Saint Cunigunda Augusta, wife and virgin of Saint Henry II Caesar, passed to the better life in the year 1040 and was buried at Bamberg in the Benedictine convent founded by her. Concerning both her and Saint Adelbert, as is read in the calendars of the Roman martyrology: the Church celebrates the feast of Saint Cunigunda on 3 March, that of Saint Henry on 15 July, and that of Saint Adelbert on 25 June.]

(Year 1018.)

[Miraeus, *Diplomatic Works*, I, 149.]

Since we know without doubt that it is pleasing in God’s sight to establish and exalt the places of the saints, in hope of divine reward, for the remedy of our soul and that of our beloved wife Cunigunda, namely the empress Augusta, and also of our parents, and likewise for confirming under divine protection [Col. 0341A] the condition of our kingdom, we grant complete freedom to the church founded by us in honor of Saint Adelbert, martyr and bishop, on the mountain adjoining our see at Aachen.

To that same church we transfer all the property within the wall called Bruell, with lands, buildings, fields, woods, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, revenues, proceeds, roads and trackless ways, and every utility that could in any way be named or written. [lacuna]

In the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1018, indiction 1, in the seventeenth year of our reign and the fifth of our empire.

Done happily at Aachen. Amen.

CIII. Saint Henry, emperor, confirms the possessions of the abbey of Saint Gislenus in Hainaut, at the request of Gerard I, bishop of Cambrai, and Roginer IV, count of Hainaut. (Year 1018.)

[Miraeus, cited above, p. 508.]

[Col. 0341B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, [Note: [Col. 0341D] Henry, a saint both in reality and by surname, was born in 972 at Abudiacum—a village and castle ten Roman miles above Regensburg, on the bank of the Danube—to Henry the Quarrelsome, duke of Bavaria, and Gisala, daughter of Conrad, king of Burgundy, and grandson of Henry, likewise duke of Bavaria and brother of the emperor Otto I, as Hermann the Lame, a writer of that period, and the compiler of the genealogy of Saint Arnulf explicitly relate. I thought this should be noted against Rader, who holds a different view in his *Holy Bavaria*. Henry, brother of the emperor Otto I, married Jutta or Judith, daughter of Arnold the Bad, duke of Bavaria. From her was born Henry the Quarrelsome, who by the aforementioned Gisala fathered Saint Henry, Bruno, bishop of Augsburg, Gisala, wife of Saint Stephen, king of Hungary, and Brigitta, abbess.] by the favor of divine clemency Roman emperor Augustus.

Wherever we assist churches established by the faithful of Christ, whether by adding something or by confirming what has been added, we do not doubt that this will benefit us and the stability of our kingdom.

Therefore let the whole company of our faithful know how we, for the remedy of our soul and of that of our lord and kinsman, namely the emperor Otto III Augustus, who undertook that venerable place under the protection of his imperial authority in order to establish God’s service there, and also through the intervention of Count Reinhard and at the petition of Gerard, venerable prelate of the Church of Cambrai, have accepted under our protection the estates granted or yet to be granted by the faithful of Christ to the poor monastery built in honor of Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, where the precious confessor of Christ, Gislenus, appears to lie bodily.

We also accept the enclosure of that place all around, namely from the River Wamy to the road where the great cross has been erected, and from there to the other stream called Aneton, so that the entire enclosure around the place, together with its jurisdiction and county, may be held as far as it reaches the great River Hagna.

[Col. 0341D] In the village of Hornud, which is recognized as lying within the same enclosure, and which blessed Gislenus perpetually possesses by the generosity of King Dagobert, we confirm by this imperial document that a market shall be held every Wednesday. We likewise confirm two parts of the village of Alemannis, [Col. 0342A] situated in the territory of Soissons. [lacuna] The same saint has possessed Alemannis from ancient times by hereditary right, through the donation of Clephontus, abbot of that place, who was a relative of King Charles. In Durno, one church; in Lismonte, one church. [lacuna]

Therefore we receive all these things under our protection, according to the custom of our predecessors. Accordingly, we strictly command that no duke, margrave, count, or any judicial person, greater or lesser, presume to disturb the monastery itself or take away any of the things belonging to it.

And so that the authority of our grant may remain firm and unshaken from now and forever, we have confirmed this command written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal. [Col. 0342B]

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus.

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erkanbald, archchaplain.

Given in indiction 1, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1018, and in the sixteenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II, the fifth of his empire.

Done happily at Nijmegen. Amen, amen, amen.

CIV. Emperor Henry grants the place called Berga, which formerly belonged to the old chapel, to the Church of Bamberg. (Year 1019, 10 May.)

[Ried, *Episcopal Codex of Regensburg*, I, 133.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, [Col. 0342C] by the grace of God Roman emperor Augustus.

Present glory is fleeting and empty while it is possessed, unless one thinks in it of something belonging to heavenly eternity. But God’s mercy has provided a useful remedy for the human race, when it made a share in the heavenly homeland the price of earthly substance.

Mindful, therefore, of this clemency, we have elevated to the dignity and see of a bishopric a certain place of our inheritance called Bamberg, established by apostolic authority and praised with the unanimous devotion of our beloved consort Cunigunda, of the venerable Henry, bishop of Würzburg, and of all our faithful—bishops, abbots, and the princes of our entire kingdom.

We founded it in pious reverence for almighty God, blessed Mary ever-virgin, the holy apostles Peter and Paul, the holy martyrs Kilian and George, and all the saints, so that there a saving sacrifice might continually be offered both for the memory of our predecessor, namely the emperor Otto III, and for that of all the faithful, living and [Col. 0343A] dead.

Therefore let all the faithful of God and of us, both the present generation and posterity to come, know how we, for the love of God and the acquisition of our salvation, grant to the aforesaid see, founded by the testimony of so many venerable men, a certain place belonging to our right called Berga, situated in the district called Tuonocgowe and in the county of Count Adalbert, which some call an abbey.

Whether it is an abbey or an estate by any other designation, by this imperial and authoritative document we grant, donate, and establish it as property, with all things belonging there, movable or immovable, cultivated or uncultivated, and every utility that can in any manner be written or named, as securely as we can, with all contradiction removed. [Col. 0343B]

Therefore we command that Eberhard, beloved by us in God and first bishop of that see, and his successors, henceforth have free power to hold, possess, exchange, or in every manner use the aforesaid abbey or estate for the benefit of the bishopric, doing whatever they wish with it.

And so that this transfer of our grant may remain firm and unshaken now and in the future, we have strengthened this document written concerning it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible emperor Augustus. (Monogram.)

Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erchanbald, archchaplain.

Given on the sixth day before the Ides of May, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation [Col. 0343C] 1019, indiction 2, in the seventeenth year of the reign of the lord Henry II and the fifth of his empire.

Done happily at Altstedt.

With the seal impressed within.

CV. Diploma of Saint Henry by which he grants two royal manses situated near Liupana, or Leuben, to the monastery of Tegernsee. (Year 1019.)

[Pez, *Diplomatic-Historical-Epistolary Codex*, from the library of Tegernsee.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God Roman emperor Augustus.

If we decide to grant assent to the worthy petitions of our faithful—namely those who approach our clemency for the condition of the kingdom, of all the Churches of God, and for the remedy of our soul and of our parents, and who ask that we strive to exalt, raise up, and enrich the churches of God’s monasteries—we hope not only to receive a reward from God himself but also believe that the condition of the kingdom is thereby exalted.

Therefore let the authority of all the holy Church of God and of our faithful recognize how, through the intervention and petition of Cunigunda, our most beloved wife and empress, and of Gotehard, our beloved abbot, we donate and grant as their own property to the monastery of Saint Quirinus, situated in the place called Tegernsee, two royal manses situated in the place called Liupana, between the two stones Watstein and Hollinstein, with buildings, cultivated and uncultivated lands, [Col. 0344A] meadows, pastures, woods, roads and trackless ways, revenues and proceeds, waters and watercourses, fisheries, acquired and to-be-acquired rights, so that the abbot of the aforesaid monastery may have free power to exchange and arrange them for the benefit of those serving God there, with every contradiction removed.

Therefore, if anyone should presume to violate or despise this document of our command, let him know that he will have to render an account to almighty God on the day of judgment and will never obtain our favor in the present age.

And so that these things may be believed more truly and more diligently observed by all, we have strengthened them with our own hand and ordered them to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of the lord Henry, most invincible and serene Roman emperor Augustus.

[Col. 0344B] Gunther, chancellor, recorded this in place of Erchenbald, archbishop and archchaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1019, indiction 2, on the fifth day before the Ides of January, and in the seventeenth year of the reign of the lord Henry and the fifth of his empire.

Done happily at Chuofunge. Amen.

CVI. Privilege of Emperor Henry concerning two manses situated near Liupana. (Year 1019.)

[Ludewig, *German Historical Writings*, p. 336]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God Roman emperor Augustus.

If we have decided to grant assent to the worthy petitions of our faithful [Col. 0344C]—that is, to those who, for the welfare of the kingdom and of all the churches of God, and for the remedy of our soul and those of our parents, approach our clemency and beseech us to strive to exalt, raise up, and enrich the churches of God’s monasteries—we hope not only to receive a reward from Him, but also consider that the welfare of the kingdom is thereby exalted. Therefore, let the diligence of all the holy Church of God and of our faithful recognize how, through the intervention and petition of Chunigunda, our most beloved wife and empress, and of Godehard, our beloved abbot, we give and grant by our own right to the monastery of Saint Quirinus, situated in the place called Tegernsee, two royal manses situated in the place called Liupana, between the two stones called Watstein [Col. 0344D] and Holinstein, with buildings, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures, woods, roads and pathless places, exits and entrances, waters and watercourses, fisheries, things sought and yet to be sought, so that the abbot of the aforesaid monastery may freely have the power to exchange and regulate them for the benefit of those serving God there, all contradiction having been removed.

Therefore, if anyone should presume to violate or despise this page of our decree, let him know that he will render an account to almighty God on the day of judgment and will never obtain our favor in the present age. And so that these things may be believed more truly and observed more diligently by all, we have confirmed them with our own hand and ordered them to be marked with the impression of our seal.

[Col. 0345A] I, Guntherius, chancellor, have examined this in place of Erchanbald, archbishop and chief chaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1019, indiction II, on the fifth day before the Ides of January, in the seventeenth year of the reign of our lord Henry and the fifth of his empire.

Done successfully at Chuofunge. Amen.

### CVII. The privilege of Saint Henry for the Church of Mimigardeford. (Year 1019.)

[Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae, p. 77.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency, emperor Augustus of the Romans.

[Col. 0345B] Wherever the venerable places of churches have been nobly enlarged by our predecessors, we confidently and truly hope to receive from almighty God, whom we honor in his saints, the reward of eternal recompense if, by our authority, we decree that they remain in their strength. Therefore, we wish it to be known to the whole of the holy Church of God and to all our faithful, present and future, how Thiederic, venerable bishop of the holy church of Mimigardeford, approached the clemency of our highness, asking that by a page of our decree we grant and confirm to his church an abbey called Liesbern, which the aforesaid church of Mimigardeford formerly appeared to possess, although without a written instrument, situated in the district of Dreni and in the county of Count Hermann.

[Col. 0345C] Assenting to his petitions as was just, and also through the intervention and petition of the empress Augusta Cunigunda, our most beloved wife, and of our other faithful who were present there—Everhard of Bamberg, Meinwerk of Paderborn, and Adalbold of Utrecht, bishops; and Duke Godefrid—we confirm and strengthen by this page of our decree, for all time, the aforesaid episcopal see, and him and his successors, so that henceforth, in the place called Liesbern, by our imperial authority they may freely have the power to order the service of God in divine love and fear.

In addition, concerning advocates in the aforesaid place, let the bishops be permitted to act and arrange the advocacy according to their will, within [Col. 0345D] their military service, in whatever way seems better to them for the benefit of the aforementioned church. And so that the authority of our decree may remain stable and unshaken for all time, confirming this page with our own hand, we have ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of our lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor Augustus of the Romans (L. M.).

Guntarius, chancellor, examined this in place of Archenbald, archbishop and chief chaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1019, indiction II, in the eighteenth year of the reign of our lord Henry and the sixth of his empire, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April.

Done successfully at Goslar.

### CVIII. Saint Henry gives the abbey of Sceldice to the Church of Paderborn. (In the same year.)

[The same, p. 78.]

[Col. 0346A]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the grace of God emperor Augustus of the Romans.

Since we know that our predecessors, kings and emperors, worked upon the supreme head, which is Christ, and that they are understood to have worked through faith in his members by enlarging churches consecrated to God or to the saints, and since we know that they thereby obtained the rewards of eternal recompense, we hope likewise to gain the joy of perpetual reward if we strive to make the holy Church of God grow and multiply in honor of its saints through gifts and additions. Therefore, we desire that it be made known to the universal Church, present and future, how Meginwerch, bishop of Paderborn and most beloved by our imperial excellence, approached our highness, asking that an abbey called Sceldice be given to his church.

[Col. 0346B] Rightly favoring his continual petitions, and through the intervention of Cunigunda, our most beloved wife and empress, as well as of the bishops Gero, Unwan, Arnold, Dietrich, Hiltiward, and Eric, and after deliberation with the nobles of our kingdom, Duke Bernhard, Count Sigifrid, Hermann, and Eggihard, we grant the aforesaid abbey, situated in the district of Wessaga and in the county of Count Friedrich, to him, to his church of Paderborn, and to his successors, to possess henceforth with every right.

So that this page of our decree may remain stable and unshaken in present and future times, we have secured it with the guarantee of our own hand and, deeming it ratified, ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of our lord Henry, most serene and unconquered emperor (L. M.).

Guntherius, chancellor, examined this in place of Erchanbald, chief chaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1018, indiction II, in the seventeenth year of the reign of our lord Henry and the sixth of his empire, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of April.

Done successfully at Goslar. Amen.

### CIX. Likewise, “a certain forest belonging to our property.” (Year 1019.)

[Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae, p. 78.]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency emperor Augustus of the Romans.

Wherever we exalt holy places of God with goods granted to us by God, we hope not only to increase the length of our life but also the prosperity of the kingdom. Therefore, let the whole community of Christ’s faithful and of our own faithful know how, for the remedy of our soul and those of our predecessors, [Col. 0347A] and also for the welfare of our beloved wife, the empress Augusta Cunigunda, and through the intervention of Gero, archbishop of Magdeburg, and of Count Doticho, we permanently and firmly give and grant to the holy church of Paderborn, over which the venerable and beloved bishop Meinwerk appears to preside, for the altar and relics of the holy Mother of God Mary, of Saint Kilian, martyr and bishop, and of Saint Liborius the confessor, a certain forest belonging to our property, situated in the county of the same Doticho, with every benefit that may in any way arise from it.

Its boundary begins beside the stream called the Fulda, near Reginhereshuson and Utenhuson, and Biberbach and Rotbrehteshuson, and extends as far as a certain river called the Wisera; from there, proceeding upward in a straight line, it reaches a certain village called Gimundin; from there, following a circuit, it returns again to the Fulda and proceeds upward as far as the aforementioned village, namely Reginhereshuson.

[Col. 0347B] And so that this authority of ours may remain stable and unshaken, strengthening it with our own hand, we have ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of our lord Henry, unconquered emperor Augustus of the Romans (L. M.).

Guntherius, chancellor, examined this in place of Erchembald, archbishop and chief chaplain.

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1018, indiction II, in the eighteenth year of the reign of our lord Henry, emperor Augustus of the Romans, and the sixth of his empire.

[Col. 0347C] Done successfully at Mulinhuson on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of January. Amen.

### CX. Saint Henry the emperor confirms by his charter to the monastery of Farfa of Saint Mary the properties newly acquired by the monks themselves, whose names are listed. (Year 1019.)

[Muratori, *Rerum Italicarum Scriptores* II, II, 513.]

Henry, by divine clemency emperor of the Romans.

Let it be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God, and let the whole community of all our faithful, present and future, know how Hugh, venerable abbot of the monastery called Farfa, belonging to the venerable Mother and Virgin of God Mary, approached our [Col. 0347D] clemency and entreated us to lend an ear to his abundant prayers—namely, that we confirm by our imperial and decretal page the properties recently acquired, by God’s favor, or wrested from the control of wicked men.

Since we ought to grant assent to all who ask what is just, by a decree of our protection we confirm to the holy monastery the properties named and listed below.

The properties that Ginizo, son of Count Hildeprand, gave to the same monastery, as contained in his deed of donation, are situated in the county of Fermo [sic]. We have likewise added, for the redemption of our soul and from our own generosity, the jurisdiction of the monastery of Spazzano, with all its appurtenances, [Col. 0348A] and the estate of Arsicio, which Ginizo has hitherto held. Just as he made our holy Lady Mary heir to his own property, so we too make her heir to our public administrative holding, lest, if we were to grant it to some secular person, they might on that occasion invade the aforesaid properties.

Also in the aforesaid county, the castle of Nova Casa, which Atto, son of Aderad, gave to it, with its appurtenances, as they are read in his charter of concession; and in another place in that county, the castle of Anganello, and the other places that Count Alker gave there, insofar as his charter records them; as well as other properties acquired in that county in recent times.

In the county of Sabina, at the place called Ortelle, the properties that John the priest gave there with his associates; [Col. 0348B] and those that Octavian and his wife Rogata offered to the aforesaid monastery in the said county, as stated in their grant; and those that Leo, son of Rezo, donated at Mojano.

Moreover, by imperial decree we order, under every form of solemn protest, that all written instruments made by Gratianus, the invader of the properties of the church of Saint Mary of Minione, which belongs to the aforesaid monastery, be broken and annulled, and that the properties return to the monastery itself without obligation.

In the county of Balva, likewise, the churches of Saint Peregrine and Saint Mary, with their appurtenances, in which Count Oderisius has recently installed monks—though they belonged to the same monastery in ancient times and have now been reacquired—which the faithful of Christ there bestowed, or which the aforesaid count recovered in whatever manner.

[Col. 0348C] Likewise, in the county of Sabina, the castle of Tribuco and another of Bucciniano, with their appurtenances, just as our lord Benedict, supreme Roman pontiff and our spiritual father, restored them to the same monastery at our request.

In the same way, those places that the aforesaid pope granted by pontifical decree for the remedy of his soul: namely, Assa within the aforesaid Bucciniano, with all its appurtenances; also the church of Saint Mary situated on the estate of Massa of Vestiario, with the estates contained in that decree.

Likewise, the church of Saint Sebastian in Collina of Flagiano, with lands and vineyards, just as that universal prelate and others granted them to the holy Mother of God by written instruments.

In the same way, the monastery of Saint Lawrence in the territory of Campania, at the place called Mac . . . , which the same venerable father offered under the aforesaid place.

[Col. 0348D] And in the county of Sabina, the land of Ortella belonging to John the priest, with churches, olive groves, and vineyards.

In the county of Rieti, the land that Transaricus granted to Saint Mary.

In the suburbs of the city of Tivoli, the monastery of Saint Adrian with all its appurtenances.

In the county of Fermo, the properties of Otto, son of Anderad, with the church of the Lord Savior, and the properties that Adelmod, son of Hildemod, gave, and whatever properties were given to the same holy Mary at Farfa by anyone.

In the city of Orte, the monastery of Saint Theodore with its churches and all its appurtenances; and the monastery of Saint Mary of Minione [Col. 0349A] with all its appurtenances, which Otto, our lord of blessed memory, restored there.

At Assisi, two churches [sic] situated on the land of the same monastery.

At Summati, the church [sic] of Saint Silvester, and the estates of the river, of the little monastery, and of Porscia.

In the county of Balva, the monastery of Saint Peregrine with all its appurtenances.

All these things, therefore, and whatever our predecessors, kings or emperors, granted to the same church of blessed Mary of Farfa, we confirm by this page, etc.

I, Piligrinus, chancellor, have examined this in place of Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg and chief chaplain.

Given in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1019, in the seventeenth year of the reign of our lord Henry and the sixth of his empire, indiction II, at Menesburgh, on the fifth day before the Ides of April.

### CXI. Saint Henry grants certain estates to Godehard, abbot of Altach. (Year 1019.)

[Ludewig, *Scriptorum rerum Germanicarum*, pp. 337–338.]

[Col. 0349B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency emperor Augustus of the Romans.

If we strive to enrich the churches of God or those serving in them with goods from our possessions, we undoubtedly believe that we shall receive an unfading reward in the future. Therefore, we wish it to be known to all our faithful, present and future, how, inflamed by desire for eternal life, both for the remedy of our soul and those of our parents, and also through the intervention of our beloved wife Cunigunda, and in return for the most pleasing service of Godehard, beloved abbot of Altach, we grant to the same church, over which he appears to preside, for the use of the monks serving God there, ten royal manses in the march and county of Margrave Adalbert.

They lie within these boundaries: on the western side, above the village called Abstorf, from the middle channel of the Danube as far as the stream called Smidaha, extending lengthwise toward the east, and lengthwise toward Wagrein, in places suitable and always useful.

[Col. 0349D] In addition, by this page of our decree we grant and bestow a small island in the Danube lying opposite the same village, with all appurtenances belonging to them: plots, buildings, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures and common pastures, roads and pathless places, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, cleared woods and woods yet to be cleared, and all implements that can be said or named.

We wholly transfer them from our imperial right into his right and lordship, on the condition that the aforesaid abbot and his successors may thereafter freely possess the power to hold, exchange, or do whatever they wish concerning them for the use of the aforesaid brothers.

And so that the authority of this donation of ours may stand stable and firm, with contradiction by all men removed, we have confirmed below with our own hand this charter written and sealed at our command.

Given on the seventh day before the Ides of April, indiction II, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1019, in the seventeenth year of the reign of our lord Henry II and the sixth of his empire.

Done successfully at Merseburg. Amen.

### CXII. Grant of the emperor Henry II concerning coinage and a market. (Year 1019, 1 July.)

[Dronke, *Codex diplomaticus Fuldensis*, p. 346.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency emperor Augustus of the Romans.

We consider it necessary, in hope of eternal reward, to exalt the venerable monasteries of divine religion with the gifts of our munificence and mercifully attend to the needs of God’s servants. Therefore, we wish it to be known to all the faithful of Christ and of ourselves how, through the intervention of our beloved wife, the empress Augusta Chunigunda, at the place called Fulda, where a monastery has been built under monastic rule in honor of the holy Mother of God Mary and the blessed martyr Boniface, in the district of Pochonia, and where we have placed the venerable and religious man Richard as its head, we grant and establish a lawful mint and a public market.

We grant to all who wish it the freedom and power to sell and buy, all contradiction and disturbance by men having been removed.

[Col. 0350C] We also give and grant by this imperial page to the aforementioned church of Fulda, as its property, the toll, jurisdiction, and everything connected with that market and mint that pertains to us by royal and imperial right, on the condition that the aforesaid abbot Richard and his successors may thereafter freely have the power to do whatever they wish, solely for the benefit of the brothers and of the Church serving God there under the rule of Saint Benedict.

And so that this authority of our grant and donation may remain stable and unshaken for all ages, we have ordered this decree, written for that purpose, to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of our lord Henry, unconquered emperor and Augustus of the Romans.

[Col. 0350D] I, Guntherius, chancellor, have examined this in place of Erkenbald, chief chaplain.

Given on the Kalends of July, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1014, in the eighteenth year of the reign of our lord Henry, emperor Augustus of the Romans, and the sixth of his empire.

Done successfully at Cologne. Amen.

### CXIII. Saint Henry gives the estate of Hammonstedi to the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1020.)

[Codex diplomaticus Historiae Westphaliae, p. 79.]

C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Henry, by the favor of divine clemency emperor Augustus of the Romans.

[Col. 0351A] We are instructed by the most salutary teachings of sacred eloquence and warned by the outstanding examples of religious men to strive to attain eternal and everlasting goods by giving temporal and earthly benefits for the love of God. Therefore, let all the faithful of Christ, present and future, know how, through the intervention of our spiritual father, namely Pope Benedict, of our most beloved wife Chunigunda, and also of Erchanbald, venerable archbishop of the church of Mainz, of our most beloved Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, and of Egilbert, bishop of Freising, and especially because of the constant and tireless service of the venerable bishop Meinwerk—so that he may not be subjected to the reproaches of any rival, but, serving us more than all others, may receive from us greater rewards and honors and, by the example of our benefit, urge others to loyal service to us—

[Col. 0351B] we give and make property, removing all contradiction, by this imperial page of our authority, to the church of Paderborn, built in honor of the holy Mother of God Mary and of Saint Kilian the martyr, and also of Saint Liborius the confessor, over which the aforementioned venerable bishop Meinwerk is known to preside, a certain estate belonging to our right, called Hammonstedi, situated in the district of Rittega and in the county of Count Uto, together with all its appurtenances and attachments, wherever they may be situated in any district or county.

That is, with villages, settlements, churches, male and female servants, plots, buildings, cultivated and uncultivated lands, roads and pathless places, exits and entrances, things sought and yet to be sought, woods, forests, hunting rights, waters, fisheries, millstones, mills, movable and immovable property, and all other benefits that can properly be written down or in any way named.

We order that the bishop M., beloved of God and often mentioned above, and his successors, thereafter freely have the power to hold and possess the same estate of Hammonstedi with all its appurtenances, or to do with it whatever they wish for the use of the bishopric.

And so that this transfer of ours may remain inviolate for all, confirming this charter written for that purpose with our own hand, we have ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

The sign of our lord Henry, emperor Augustus of the Romans (L. M.).

[Col. 0351D] I, Guntherius, chancellor, have examined this in place of Erchanbald, chief chaplain.

Given on the ninth day before the Kalends of May, on the feast of Saint George the martyr, indiction III, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1020, in the nineteenth year of the reign of our lord Henry II and the seventh of his empire. Done at Bamberg.
