If, therefore, in this life we anticipate him and become accusers of our own crime, we shall escape the wickedness of the devil, our enemy and accuser, as Paul testifies when he says: “If we judged ourselves, we would certainly not be judged.”

### CHAPTER 5.—The priest, seeing him ashamed, should continue:

Perhaps, dearest brother, not everything you have done comes to your memory at present. I will question you. Take care not to presume, at the devil’s prompting, to conceal anything.

Then he should question him in the following order.

[Col. 0951C]

Have you voluntarily committed homicide, without necessity, not against an enemy, but out of greed, so that you might take away what belonged to him, and thus killed him? If you have, you must do penance for forty continuous days—which the common people call a *carina*—fasting on bread and water, and you must observe the following seven years according to this rule.

For the first year after those forty days, you must abstain entirely from wine, *medo* [mead], lard, cheese, and every fatty fish, except on those feast days that are celebrated by the whole people in that bishopric. If you are on a long journey, in a military expedition, at a royal court, or held by some illness, you may then redeem Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday by one denarius, or the value of one denarius, or by feeding three poor persons. Even so, you may use only one of the three things mentioned above—that is, you may drink either wine, or mead, or honeyed beer.

After you return home or are restored to health, you shall have no permission to redeem. When the year has been completed, you shall be brought into the church and the kiss of peace shall be granted to you.

In the second and third years, you shall fast in the same way, except that you shall have the power to redeem Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at the previously mentioned price wherever you are. Observe all the other requirements carefully, as in the first year.

During each of the four remaining years, you must fast three Lents on the appointed weekdays. The first is before Easter, with the other Christians; the second before the feast of Saint John the Baptist; and, if anything remains, you shall complete it afterward. The third is before the Nativity of the Lord. During it, abstain from wine, mead, honeyed beer, meat, lard, cheese, and fatty fish.

In the four years mentioned above, you may take whatever you wish on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. You may redeem Monday and Wednesday at the price already stated. You must always observe Friday on bread and water. When these matters have been completed, you shall receive holy communion, but in such a way that you do not live without penance as long as you live. Throughout your whole life, do penance every Friday on bread and water; and, if you wish to redeem it, you shall have the power to do so with one denarius, or the value of one denarius, or by feeding three poor persons.

We grant these things to you according to mercy, not according to the strictness of the canons, because the canons prescribe this: “If anyone commits homicide deliberately and out of greed, let him abandon the world, enter a monastery of monks, and serve God there continually.”

Have you committed homicide in revenge for your parents? Do penance for forty days, called a *carina*, together with the following seven years, because the Lord says: “Vengeance is mine, and I will repay.”

If you committed homicide unwillingly, intending in your anger to strike someone but not to kill him, and nevertheless killed him, do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and for the following seven years. But during the first year you may redeem Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, each separately with one denarius or the value of one denarius, or by feeding three poor persons. Observe the remaining six years as it has been established for homicides committed voluntarily.

Did you commit homicide in war at the command of a lawful ruler, who ordered it to be done for the sake of peace, and did you kill a tyrant who was striving to destroy the peace? Do penance for three Lents on the appointed weekdays. But if it was otherwise—that is, without the command of a lawful ruler—do penance for it as for voluntary homicide: one *carina* together with the following seven years.

[Col. 0952D]

As a free man, did you kill your lord’s slave, who had committed no offense against you, but did so at your lord’s command? Do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, together with the following seven years; and your lord must do the same, unless the slave was a thief or robber and the lord ordered it to be done for the peace of others.

But if you, as a slave, killed your fellow slave at the command of your master, your master must do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, together with the following seven years; and you must do three Lents on the appointed weekdays, except if it was done for the common peace.

Did you advise someone to commit homicide but did not carry it out, and was a person killed because of that advice? Do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, together with the following seven years.

Did you investigate or spy on someone and thereby deliver him into the hands of his enemies, and was he killed? Do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and observe the following seven years in the customary manner.

Were you with others who fought against someone, either in your own house, in another person’s house, or in some place where he had hoped to defend himself; and did you throw a stone at him, or shoot an arrow or some kind of dart against him, intending to kill him, but he was neither struck nor wounded by you, while nevertheless he was killed by others with whom you were attacking him? Do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and observe the following seven years in the customary manner.

You committed parricide—that is, you killed your father, mother, brother, sister, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, maternal aunt, paternal aunt, or did something similar. If it happened accidentally, not willingly, and you did not intend to strike in anger, but the event occurred by chance, you must do penance as for a homicide committed deliberately. But if you did it intentionally and in anger, you must observe this discipline: for the course of one year you must persevere in prayer before the doors of the basilica, imploring the Lord’s mercy. When the year has been completed, you shall be admitted into the church. Nevertheless, you must stand in a corner of the church until the period of one year has come to an end. When these things have been carried out, if the fruit of penance is seen in you, you may partake of the Lord’s body and blood, lest you be hardened by despair. You shall not eat meat for all the days of your life. [Col. 0953C] You shall fast daily until the ninth hour, except on feast days and Sundays. You shall abstain from wine, mead, and honeyed beer for three days each week. You shall not dare to bear arms, except against pagans. Wherever you wish to go, you shall not be conveyed in any vehicle, but shall proceed on your own feet. You shall not separate from your wife, if you have one; but if you have none, you shall not take another. The duration of this penance shall be at the discretion of your bishop, so that, according to your conduct, he may be able either to extend or to shorten it.

You committed a homicide by accident, without wishing to kill anyone or intending to strike anyone in anger, whether with a staff, an iron weapon, or any kind of scourge, but were simply going somewhere—or into the forest to hunt—and wished to shoot a wild animal, [Col. 0953D] and thus, unexpectedly, without your wanting or knowing it, you killed a person instead of the animal?

Or, if you were playing some game with others and, in the course of play, wished to strike some object—a little bird or some other animal—or something with an arrow, stick, or stone, and thus killed either your brother, your son, or some other person;

Or, if you were standing in a public place, or in your own courtyard, or somewhere else, and for amusement threw a stone toward a place where you saw no one and had laid no ambush, yet nevertheless killed someone;

Or, if someone had compelled you to play with him, and you were the stronger and threw him down beneath you—or he threw you down—and he died after being wounded by your knife or his own;

[Col. 0954A] Or, if, while you were occupied with necessary work, an axe flew from your hand, or an iron tool slipped from its handle and struck your companion and friend, who was killed: if you have done these things, or anything similar, and harbored no evil intention against the persons mentioned above or against people like them, you shall fast for forty days—in the manner customary, which the common people call a *carina*—and do penance for the following five years. During these five years, abstinence from food shall be relaxed mercifully, so that in the first year you may redeem the three fast days—the third day, the fifth day, and Saturday—for one denarius, or the value of one denarius, or by feeding three poor people. In another year you may have the power [Col. 0954B] to redeem all the fast days, except Friday, on which you must always fast on bread and water, at the aforesaid price. Thus you must observe the remaining years.

But if you were going with your brother or companion into the forest to cut wood, and, as a tree was about to fall, you told your brother or companion to flee, and he was crushed beneath the tree while fleeing, you shall be innocent of his death.

But if, through your carelessness or negligence, while he was felling another tree beside you, you did not warn him in time so that he could foresee the tree’s fall, and thus through your negligence he was crushed and died, then you must do penance as a homicide, though much more lightly than for what was done intentionally.

Did you kill your superior, or take part in a council [Col. 0954C] so that he would be killed, or kill your wife, a part of your own body? We propose two courses of penance to you; choose whichever of the two is dearer to you. The first is this: abandon this fragile world, enter a monastery, and humble yourself under the authority of the abbot; faithfully observe everything he commands you.

The second course is this: lay down your arms and abandon all worldly business. Do not eat meat or fat for all the days of your life, except on one day of the Lord’s Resurrection, one day of Pentecost, and one day of the Lord’s Nativity. At other times do penance on bread and water, and sometimes on legumes and vegetables. Persevere at all [Col. 0954D] times in fasts, vigils, prayers, and almsgiving. Never drink wine, mead, or honeyed beer, except on those three days mentioned above. Do not take a wife, do not keep a concubine, and do not commit adultery; remain forever without hope of marriage. Never wash yourself in a bathhouse, do not mount a horse, and do not pursue your own or another’s case in the assembly of the faithful. Never sit at the banquets of those who are rejoicing. In church, separated from the other Christians, stand humbly behind the door. Earnestly commend yourself to the prayers of those entering and leaving. Consider yourself unworthy of receiving the communion of the Lord’s holy body and blood for all the days of your life. But at the final end of your life, we grant you permission to receive it as viaticum, if you have observed this discipline.

Did you kill, or take part in a council to have killed, [Col. 0955A] a penitent who was doing public penance and was wearing the very clothing or habit customary for those who fast a *carina*? If you have done this, you must fast for what he had begun, and observe in full what was prescribed above for those who committed homicides deliberately and out of desire.

Did you cut off someone’s hands or feet, tear out your brother’s eyes, or wound someone? For mutilation, because you made your neighbor and brother disabled and useless to himself—unless you did it for theft, robbery, or the common peace—you must do severe penance for one year. For wounds, if the wound is serious and has left disfiguring scars, because you made your neighbor and brother disfigured, you must do penance for forty days on bread and water. [Col. 0955B]

Did you kill a thief or robber when he could have been captured without being killed, and nevertheless killed him? Since he was created in the image of God, baptized in his name, and redeemed by his blood, you shall not enter the church for forty days. During those days, dressed in a woolen garment, abstain from the forbidden foods and drinks, from sexual intercourse, from the sword, and from riding. On Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, use some kind of legumes, vegetables and fruits, or small fish, with a moderate amount of beer, and do so temperately. But if, without consideration of hatred, you killed a member of the devil in order to free yourself and your possessions, I speak according to mercy: because of the image of God, if you wish to fast at all, it is good for you, and give alms generously. [Col. 0955C] If a priest has done the same, he shall not be deposed; nevertheless, as long as he lives, he shall do penance.

Did you accuse someone, and was he killed through your accusation, unless it was for the sake of peace? You must do penance for forty days on bread and water, which is called a *carina*, together with the following seven years. But if he was weakened through your denunciation, you must do penance for three forty-day periods on the customary fast days.

Did you seize someone and hand him over to a place where either he was killed or his limbs were cut off? You must fast in the same manner, even if you say that you did not hand him over there for the purpose of having him weakened or killed.

[Col. 0955D] Did you yourself kill, or did someone kill on your advice, one of the ecclesiastical men dedicated to God—a psalmist, doorkeeper, reader, exorcist, acolyte, subdeacon, deacon, or priest? If you have done this, you must do penance separately for each order and each rank. You must proceed as follows: for a psalmist, forty days on bread and water—which is called *carina* in the Teutonic language—together with the following seven years. The same applies to a doorkeeper, the same to a reader, the same to an exorcist, the same to an acolyte, the same to a subdeacon, the same to a deacon, and the same to a priest, because every priest has eight orders. Therefore, whoever deliberately kills a priest must do penance as for eight homicides committed deliberately, and must never be without penance. [Col. 0956A] Nevertheless, according to the council of Worms, you must do penance as follows: if you deliberately kill a priest, you shall not eat meat or drink wine for all the days of your life. Fast daily until evening, except on feast days and Sundays. Do not bear arms, do not mount a horse, and do not enter a church for five years, but stand before the church doors. After five years enter the church, but do not yet receive communion; stand or sit in a corner of the church. When the twelfth year has been completed, permission to receive communion shall be granted to you, and remission shall be granted for riding. In the remaining disciplines, however, you shall continue to observe three days each week, so that you may deserve to be purified more perfectly.

## Concerning perjury

[Col. 0956B] Did you commit perjury out of greed? Fast for forty days on bread and water, which the common people call a *carina*, and observe the following seven years in the customary manner. As long as you live, fast every Friday on bread and water. If you wish to redeem this, you may do so for one denarius, or the value of one denarius, or by feeding three poor people. Nevertheless, the Roman Penitential prescribes: if anyone swears falsely out of greed, let him sell all his possessions and distribute them to the poor; then, having entered a monastery, let him submit himself to perpetual penance.

Did you knowingly commit perjury and lead others into perjury? You must do penance for forty days on bread and water, which the common people call a *carina*, and observe the following seven years in the customary manner. [Col. 0956C] You must fast for as many perjuries as there were people whom you knowingly led into perjury, and they themselves must make satisfaction for their perjuries, as noted above, if they acted knowingly. Otherwise, the penance is lighter.

Did you commit perjury under compulsion, out of necessity, or for the sake of your life? Because you loved your body more than your soul, you must do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and do penance on bread and water on every Friday occurring within one year; you may not redeem this.

## Concerning idle oaths

Did you swear fidelity to a prostitute or adulteress, or make some similar promise under oath that was contrary to canon law? Do penance for the oath, [Col. 0956D] and break it. This is better and more just than remaining in sexual depravity or some other evil, because it is written: “Unjust vows must be broken.”

If you swore by God’s hair, or by his head, or used blasphemy against God in some other way, and did it once unknowingly, do penance for seven days on bread and water. If, after being reproved, you did it a second or third time, do penance for fifteen days on bread and water. If you swore by heaven or earth, by the sun or moon, or by any other creature, do penance for fifteen days on bread and water.

If you bound yourself by an oath never to return to peace with one of your enemies, then, for perjury, remain separated from the body and blood of the Lord for one year, [Col. 0957A] and do penance for forty days on bread and water. But return quickly to charity, which covers a multitude of sins.

If you determined or firmly bound yourself by an oath to do something that would not please God, do penance according to the measure of the sin, and let what you rashly and unjustly determined be revoked. If it happened that you swore something heedlessly, and its observance would lead to a worse outcome, we decree, in accordance with synodal decisions, that it must be changed, rather than that, by remaining bound to the oath, you should turn aside into a greater crime.

## Concerning theft

Did you steal something from the ecclesiastical treasury inside a church—gold, silver, gems, books, altar cloths, or priestly [Col. 0957B] vestments; veils, carpets, or anything given or made for the use of the church? If you did, return what you took and do penance for three *carinae* together with the following seven years. If you stole the sacred relics themselves, return the sacred objects and fast for seven *carinae*.

If you broke into a Christian’s house by night and took his four-footed animals—that is, a horse, ox, or other animals—or something of greater value worth forty solidi, return the price and do penance for one year on the customary fast days. If you do not return it, do penance for two years on the customary fast days. If you committed a greater theft, you must do greater penance. If you did it repeatedly, [Col. 0957C] you must increase the penance all the more. If you committed a small theft, do penance for ten days on bread and water; children shall do penance for five days on bread and water.

## Concerning robbery

If you committed robbery, you must do more severe penance, because it is more pitiable that you robbed someone by force while he was watching than that you stole from him while he was sleeping or absent. If you committed theft out of necessity—that is, if you had nothing from which to live and, because of hunger, stole only food outside a church, and did not do it from habit—return what you took and do penance for three Fridays on bread and water. But if you cannot return it, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

## Concerning adultery

[Col. 0957D]

Did you commit adultery with another man’s wife while you yourself had no wife? Do penance for forty days on bread and water, which in common speech is called a *carina*, together with the following seven years.

If, as a married man, you committed adultery with another man’s wife, because you had a way to satisfy your lust, you must do penance for two *carinae* together with the following fourteen years: one because you had another woman in addition to your wife—there is one adultery—and another because you had another man’s wife—there is a second adultery. You must never be without penance.

## Concerning fornication

If, being unmarried, you committed fornication with an unmarried woman, [Col. 0958A] do penance for ten days on bread and water; if with your own female slave, do penance likewise.

If you dismissed your wife and took another, take back your former wife and do penance for one *carina* on bread and water together with the following seven years, because it is written: “What God has joined, let no human being separate.” No one is permitted to dismiss his wife except on account of fornication—that is, if she has committed adultery with another man. Then he may dismiss her because of fornication, but while she lives he may not take another wife. But if they wish to remain separated in such a way that neither brings a complaint against the other concerning the separation, let them remain so. If, however, they bring complaints against one another concerning the separation, then, after penance has been completed between them [Col. 0958B]—namely, after seven years of penance—the bishop must reconcile them if they ask. The same law applies to a husband in relation to his wife if he himself has committed adultery; and if she wishes, she may dismiss her husband because of fornication, according to the same rule stated above concerning a wife who commits adultery.

Did you take a wife without celebrating a public wedding, and did neither you nor your wife come to the church, and did you not receive a blessing from the priest as prescribed in the canons, and did you not endow her with whatever dowry you could—a piece of land, movable goods, gold, silver, slaves, animals, or according to your means—finally, even a denarius, or the value of a denarius, or the value of an obol, simply so that she would be endowed? If you did not do this, you must do penance for three forty-day periods on the customary fast days. [Col. 0958C]

Did you commit fornication with a nun—that is, with Christ’s bride? If you did, do penance for forty days on bread and water, which is called a *carina*, together with the following seven years, and, as long as you live, observe every Friday on bread and water.

If you corrupted a virgin and afterward took her as your wife, because you violated the one thing that is greatest—the marriage itself—do penance for one year on the customary fast days. But if you did not take her as your wife after corrupting her, do penance for two years on the customary fast days.

Did you take as your wife a woman whom another man had betrothed to himself? [Col. 0958D] Dismiss her, because she can never become your legitimate wife, and do penance for forty days on bread and water, which is called a *carina*, together with the following seven years.

Did you seize your wife and carry her away by force, without the consent of the woman or of the parents under whose guardianship she was? If you did this, according to the authority of the canons you may neither keep her nor ever take another wife. But if she did not consent, she has permission in the Lord to marry. You, however, must do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and for the following seven years. And because legitimate marriages are established by God’s command, because by God’s command two bodies are made one, and because a legitimate marriage must not be contracted except by the consent of both parties and their parents, you, who disturbed and violated that holy institution, must remain without hope of marriage. [Col. 0959A]

Did it happen that your wife, with your knowledge and encouragement, committed adultery with another man, although she herself was unwilling? If you did this, do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, and for seven years, one of those years on bread and water, and never be without penance. But if your wife can prove that, through your fault and at your command, she committed adultery while resisting and unwilling, then, if she cannot remain continent, let her marry whomever she wishes, provided it is in the Lord. You, however, must remain forever without hope of a wife. But if she had consented, let her fast the same fasts prescribed for you and remain without hope of marriage.

[Col. 0959B] Did you take as your wife a female relative of yours, or a woman whom one of your relatives had had? You must separate from her and do penance according to the degree of kinship, because the holy Fathers and their holy statutes reserve absolutely no pardon for incestuous unions and do not define a number of generations. Rather, they established that no Christian may take a wife from his own blood relationship or kinship for as long as the lineage can be recalled, recognized, or kept in memory. For Saint Gregory says: “If anyone takes into marriage a woman from his own kinship, or one whom his kinsman had had, let him be anathema.”

Therefore, you must know that the matter is not as many priests deceive many people by saying—that penance can exist while one remains in the very sin. [Col. 0959C] For example, if you now had your female relative, or another man’s wife, or something similar that was not lawful, and wished to remain in that sin while nevertheless being in penance; for example, if today you had completed forty days on bread and water in penance for some sin and then repeated the earlier sin, the penance you had done would be of no value, in accordance with what is said: “As a dog returns to its vomit, and a sow to its wallowing,” so it will be with the sinner who returns to a sin previously confessed. Therefore know truly that, while you remain in that sin, the penance for that same sin is of no value.

## Concerning abuse of marriage

Did you have intercourse with your wife or with some other woman from behind, like a dog? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and [Col. 0959D] water.

Did you join yourself to your wife during her menstrual period? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and water. If your wife entered the church before her blood had been purified after childbirth, let her do penance for as many days as she ought to have remained absent from the church. But if you had intercourse with her during those days, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you have intercourse with your wife after the infant had moved in the womb, or at least within forty days before childbirth? If you did, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you have intercourse with your wife after the conception had become evident? Do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0960A] Did you have intercourse with your wife on Sunday? You must do penance for four days on bread and water.

Did you defile yourself with your wife during Lent? You must do penance for forty days on bread and water, or give twenty-six solidi as alms. If it happened through drunkenness, do penance for twenty days on bread and water. You must preserve chastity during the twenty days before the Nativity of the Lord, on every Sunday, throughout all prescribed fasts, on the feasts of the apostles, and on the principal and public feast days. If you did not preserve it, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

## Concerning false testimony

Did you give false testimony—that is, did you testify and affirm that something false was true—and did you do this out of love for someone, whether for a reward [Col. 0960B] or through fear? If you did, you must do penance as for adultery and for homicides committed deliberately, since the Lord says: “For out of the heart come homicides, adulteries, thefts, false testimonies.” Therefore a false witness must likewise do penance and be excommunicated, as an adulterer, thief, and homicide. But if you did it out of fear of someone whom you might have feared because he could cause you to lose your limbs, your life, or finally your possessions, then divide the penance, and afterward take care that this does not happen to you again.

## Concerning magic

Did you violate a grave—that is, while seeing someone being buried, did you break open the grave at night and take his clothing? If you did, do penance for two years on the customary fast days. [Col. 0960C]

Did you consult magicians and bring them into your house to investigate something by magical arts, or for the purpose of purification; or, following pagan custom, did you summon diviners to tell your future, as though you were seeking it from a prophet; or invite those who practice sortes, those who hope through sortes to foresee the future, or those who serve auguries or incantations? If you did, do penance for two years on the customary fast days.

If you observed pagan traditions which, as though by hereditary right and with the devil supplying them, fathers have always handed down to their sons until the present day—that is, if you worshiped the elements, the moon, the sun, or the course of the stars; the new moon or an eclipse of the moon, so that by your shouts or assistance you might restore its brightness, or so that those elements might help you or you might help them; or if you observed the new moon when building a house or joining a marriage—if you did this, do penance for two years on the customary fast days, because it is written: “Whatever you do in word or deed, do everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” [Col. 0960D]

Did you observe the Kalends of January according to pagan custom, doing something more because of the new year than you had done before or afterward? That is, did you prepare your table with stones or banquets in your house at that time; lead singers and choruses through the streets and public ways; or sit upon the roof of your house, encircled with your sword, so that there you might see and understand what would happen to you in the coming year? Or did you sit at a crossroads upon a bull’s hide so that there too you might understand the future? Or did you have loaves baked in your name on the aforementioned night, so that, if they rose well and became thick and high, you might foresee from them the prosperity of your life in that year? Because you abandoned God your creator and turned to idols and those vanities, becoming an apostate, do penance for two years on the customary fast days. [Col. 0961A]

Did you make bindings, incantations, and the various enchantments that wicked men—swineherds, cowherds, and sometimes hunters—make, while they recite diabolical songs over bread, herbs, or certain wicked bindings, and either hide these in a tree or throw them at a crossroads or place where three roads meet, so that they might free their own animals or dogs from disease and destruction and bring loss upon another’s? If you did, do penance for two years on the customary fast days.

Did you take part in, or consent to, the vanities that women practice in their spinning and weaving—when they begin their webs, hoping through incantations and their practices (*aggressu*, uncertain) to make both the warp and the weft become so entangled with one another [Col. 0961B] that everything will perish unless they counteract it with other diabolical incantations? If you took part or consented, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

Did you gather medicinal herbs with other incantations, together with the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer—that is, while singing “I believe in God” and “Our Father”? If you did it otherwise, do penance for ten days on bread and water. [Col. 0961C]

Did you go to some place to pray other than a church or another religious place designated for you by your bishop or priest—that is, to springs, stones, trees, or crossroads—and there light a candle or torch in veneration of the place, or bring bread or some offering there, or eat there, or seek there some healing of body or soul? If you did this, or consented to it, do penance for three years on the customary fast days.

Did you seek sortes in books or on tablets, as many people are accustomed to do when they presume to cast sortes in psalters, Gospels, or other such things? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and water. [Col. 0961D]

Did you ever believe, or take part in that perfidy, that enchanters and those who claim to be senders of storms could, through the enchantment of demons, stir up storms or change people’s minds? If you believed this or took part in it, do penance for one year on the customary fast days.

Did you believe, or take part in that unbelief, that there is some woman who can, through certain magical practices and incantations, change people’s minds—from hatred to love or from love to hatred—or through her enchantments condemn or steal away people’s goods? If you believed this or took part in it, [Col. 0962A] do penance for one year on the customary fast days.

Did you believe that there is some woman who can do what certain women, deceived by the devil, claim that they must necessarily and by command do—that is, ride on certain nights upon certain beasts with a host of demons transformed into the likeness of women, and count herself among their company? The common folly calls this woman *holda*. If you took part in that unbelief, you must do penance for one year on the customary fast days.

## Concerning sacrilege

Did you curse your father or mother, beat them, or dishonor them in any way? If you did, do penance for forty days—one *carina*—on bread and water, together with the following seven years, because the Lord said: “Whoever curses his father or mother shall die the death.” [Col. 0962B]

Did you take something from the ecclesiastical treasury? If you did, restore fourfold, or do penance for three years on the customary fast days.

Did you lead, send, or sell someone into captivity, unless it was for the sake of the common peace? If you did, bring him back if you can; if not, do penance for two years on the customary fast days.

Did you burn another person’s house or property out of hatred? If you did, repay the damage and do penance for one year on the customary fast days.

## Concerning contempt for fasting

Did you break the Lenten fast before the evening office had been celebrated, except on account of illness? If you did, for each day you must do penance for three days on bread and water, because the canons prescribe that during Lent one should hurry to Mass and, after hearing the solemnities of the Mass and the evening offices and giving alms, approach food. But if someone is compelled by necessity and cannot come to church or hear Mass, let him, when the evening hour has been reckoned and the prayer completed, break his fast. [Col. 0962C]

Did you despise a fast enjoined by the holy Church and refuse to observe it with the other Christians? Do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you break the Ember fast and fail to observe it with the other Christians? Do penance for forty days on [Col. 0962D] bread and water.

Did you fast on Sunday out of abstinence and religious devotion? Do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

If you did not observe the fast of the Greater Litanies, the Rogation days, and the vigils of the saints, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you publicly compel a penitent to eat and drink beyond what had been commanded him, unless you gave alms for him at that time? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you despise someone while you were fasting who could not fast and was eating? If you did, do penance for five days on bread and water.

Did you break the fast on Maundy Thursday and Holy Saturday so that you would eat more frequently on those two days than on the other days of Lent, except at the evening meal or because of illness? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and water. [Col. 0963A]

## Concerning gluttony and drunkenness

Did you make a habit of eating and drinking more than was necessary for you? If you did, do penance for ten days on bread and water, because the Lord says in the Gospel: “See to it that your hearts are not weighed down with debauchery and drunkenness.”

Did you ever drink so much that you vomited because of drunkenness? If you did, do penance for fifteen days on bread and water.

Did you ever make yourself drunk out of boastfulness—that is, boasting that you could outdrink others—and thus, through your vanity and encouragement, lead yourself and others into drunkenness? If you did, [Col. 0963B] do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

Did you vomit the body and blood of the Lord because of drunkenness? If you did, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

If you made someone else drunk through wickedness, do penance for twenty days on bread and water. If through good will, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

## Concerning irreligious conduct

Did you neglect to receive the Lord’s body and blood at these four times—that is, on Maundy Thursday, Easter, Pentecost, and the Nativity of the Lord—and did you fail to abstain from intercourse throughout Lent, and afterward, at the other times mentioned above, for either seven or five days before receiving the Lord’s holy body? If you neglected these things, you must do penance for twenty days on bread and water. [Col. 0963C]

Did you reject the Mass, prayer, or the offering of a married priest—that is, did you refuse to confess your sins to him or to receive the Lord’s body and blood from him because he appeared to you to be a sinner? If you did, do penance for one year on the customary fast days.

## Again, concerning magic

Did you believe, or take part in that unbelief, that certain wicked women, turned backward after Satan and deceived by demonic illusions and phantasms, believe and profess that during the hours of night they ride with Diana, the pagan goddess, and with an innumerable multitude of women upon certain beasts, passing over great stretches of land in the silence of the dead of night, obeying her commands as though she were their mistress, and being summoned to her service on certain nights? But would that these women alone had perished in their unbelief and had not dragged many with them into the destruction of unbelief! For an innumerable multitude, deceived by this false opinion, believes these things to be true; and by believing, turns away from the right faith and rolls about in pagan error, since it imagines that some divinity or divine power exists apart from the one God. [Col. 0963D]

For the devil transforms himself into the forms and likenesses of various persons, and, deceiving in dreams the mind he holds captive, shows it now joyful things, now sad things, now unknown persons, and leads it through every kind of byway. When only the spirit suffers this, the faithless mind supposes that it happens not in the mind but in the body. For who is not carried outside himself in dreams and nocturnal visions, and sees while sleeping many things that he has never seen while awake? Who, however, is so foolish and dull as to think that all these things, which occur only in the spirit, also happen in the body? The prophet Ezekiel saw and heard the Lord’s visions in the spirit, not in the body, as he himself says: “Immediately,” he says, “I was in the spirit.” And Paul does not dare to say that he was caught up in the body. [Col. 0964A]

Therefore it must be publicly announced to everyone that whoever believes such things and things like them loses the faith; and whoever does not have the right faith in God is not God’s, but belongs to the one in whom he believes—that is, the devil. For it is written concerning our Lord: [Col. 0964B] “All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made.” If you believed these vanities, do penance for two years on the customary fast days.

Did you observe funeral vigils—that is, did you attend the watch over dead bodies where the bodies of Christians were guarded according to pagan custom—and sing diabolical songs there, perform the dances that pagans invented under the devil’s instruction, drink there, break into loud laughter, and, setting aside all piety and the feeling of charity, appear to rejoice as though at the death of a brother? If you did, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

## Concerning superstition

Did you make diabolical amulets or diabolical characters, which some people make at the devil’s prompting, or use herbs or amber; or did you honor Thursday in honor of Jupiter? If you did this or consented to it, do penance for forty days on bread and water. [Col. 0964C]

Did you conspire with other plotters against your bishop or against his fellow workers—that is, did you mock or deride the teaching or commands of your bishop or priest? If you did, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

Did you eat anything from an idol offering—that is, from offerings made in certain places at the graves of the dead, or at springs, trees, stones, or crossroads—or did you carry stones onto a mound, or carry head-bindings to crosses set up at crossroads? If you did this, or consented to any of these practices, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

### Also concerning magical practices

Did you send your son or daughter onto a roof or onto an oven for the sake of some healing; or burn grains where a dead person had been; or tie the belt of a dead person into knots to cause someone harm; or strike together over a funeral the combs with which women commonly tease wool; or, when a funeral was being carried out of the house, split a wagon in two and have the funeral carried through the middle of the wagon’s division? If you did this, or consented to it, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you perform or consent to the superstitious practices that foolish women commonly perform—when the corpse of a dead person still lies in the house, they run to the water, secretly bring back a vessel of water, and, when the dead body is lifted, pour that same water beneath the bier; and they observe this while the funeral is carried outside the house, so that the body may not be lifted higher than the knees, doing this for the sake of some healing? If you did this or consented to it, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you do or consent to what some do for a slain man when he is buried? They give him a certain ointment in his hand, as though by that ointment the wound could be healed after death, and so bury him with the ointment. If you did this, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you do or say anything, in any work that you began through divination or magical art, without invoking the name of God? If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0965B] Did you do anything like what the pagans did and still do on the Kalends of January, in the “little deer” (*cervulus*) or the “little heifer” (*vegula*)? If you did this, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

Did you slander or curse anyone out of envy? If you did this, you must do penance for seven days on bread and water.

Did you do what many people do? They sweep the place where they customarily make a fire in their house and throw barley grains onto the still-warm spot. If the grains leap, it will be dangerous; but if they remain there, it will be favorable. If you did this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you do what some people do when they visit a sick person? When they approach the house where the sick person lies, if they find a stone lying nearby, they turn the stone over and look in the place where it lay to see whether something living is underneath. If they find a worm, fly, ant, or anything that moves, they then declare that the sick person will recover. But if they find nothing there that moves, they say that the sick person will die. If you did this or believed it, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you make little childish bows and children’s sewing implements, and throw them either into your cellar or into your barn so that satyrs or hairy spirits might play with them there, bring you the possessions of others, and make you richer thereby? If you did this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0965D] Did you do what some people do on the Kalends of January—that is, on the eighth day after the Nativity of the Lord? On that holy night they spin, weave, sew, and begin every kind of work they can begin, urged on by the devil, in honor of the new year. If you did this, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

### Also concerning adultery

Did you have intercourse with your wife’s sister? If you did this, you may have neither woman. If the woman who was your wife was not aware of the crime, then, if she does not wish to remain continent, let her marry in the Lord whomsoever she wishes. But you and the adulteress must remain without hope of marriage and, for as long as you live, perform penance according to the priest’s instructions.

If, while your wife was absent, your wife’s sister entered your bed without your knowledge and without your wife’s knowledge, and you thought that she was your wife and had intercourse with her, then, after completing your penance, you may have a lawful marriage. But she, the adulteress, must be punished as worthy of retribution and be deprived of marriage forever.

### Also concerning fornication

Did you commit fornication with two sisters, when the one sister did not know that the other had been violated by you, and you did not know that the second woman was the sister of the first? If you did this, you must do penance for seven years during the prescribed penitential periods; afterward you may enter a lawful marriage. And those sisters, if they perform worthy penance and are unable to remain continent, may marry in the Lord. But if they were not unaware of the matter, let them do penance until death and abstain from marriage.

[Col. 0966B] Did you commit fornication with a woman, and, with your knowledge, did your brother afterward marry that same woman? If you did this, because you concealed the crime from your brother, do penance for seven years during the prescribed penitential periods; after your penance, both you and your brother may take wives, but only in the Lord. The woman, however, must do penance until death and remain without hope of marriage.

Did you commit fornication with your stepdaughter? If you did this, you may have neither the mother nor the daughter; you may not take a wife, nor may she take a husband. Rather, you must both do penance until death. But your wife, if, after learning that you had committed adultery with her daughter, she did not have intercourse with you, may marry in the Lord if she wishes.

[Col. 0966C] Did you commit fornication with your stepmother? If you did this, neither you nor she may thereafter enter into marriage. Your father, however, may take another wife if he wishes.

Did you commit fornication with your brother’s wife? If you did this, you and she must do penance until death and remain without hope of marriage. Your brother, however, may take another wife if he wishes.

Did you commit fornication with your son’s betrothed, and did your son afterward marry her? If you did this, because you concealed the crime from your son, do penance until death and remain without hope of marriage. Your son, since he was unaware of your sin, may take another wife if he wishes. She, however, after completing her penance, must remain without hope of marriage.

[Col. 0966D] Did you commit fornication with your mother? If you did this, do penance for fifteen years during the prescribed penitential periods, one of those years on bread and water; remain without hope of marriage, and never be without penance. But your mother, if she did not consent, should do penance according to the priest’s judgment; and, if she does not wish to remain continent, let her marry in the Lord.

Did you commit fornication with your godmother? If you did this, you must separate from her and do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, followed by seven years of penance.

Did you commit fornication with your spiritual daughter, whom you had received from the font or held in your hands before the bishop? If you did this, you must separate from her and do penance for forty days, called a *carina*, [Col. 0967A] followed by seven years of penance.

### Concerning the dissolution of marriage

Did you hold your son, daughter, stepson, or stepdaughter for confirmation, or receive one of them from the font, with the intention of causing a separation between yourself and your wife? If the bishop is unwilling to give another ruling in the matter, you must then separate from your wife and do penance for forty days, called a *carina*, on bread and water, followed by seven years of penance. You must never be without penance and must remain without hope of marriage. Your wife, if she cannot remain continent, may marry in the Lord.

Did you take a woman and keep her for some time—a month, three months, or finally a year—and only then say that you were of a cold nature, so that you could not have intercourse with her or with any other woman? And if the woman who was to be your wife affirms the same thing that you do, and it can be established by a proper judgment that matters are as you say, you may separate, but on this condition: if you afterward take another wife, you are to be judged guilty of perjury, and, after completing your penance, you must renew your former marriage.

But if she first appealed to the bishop or his envoy after a year or a year and a half, saying that you had not known her and denying that any intercourse had taken place between you, while you affirm that she is your wife, you are to be believed, because you are the head of the woman. For if she wished to make an appeal, why did she remain silent for so long? A woman could quickly and in a short time know whether you were able to have intercourse with her. But if, immediately at the beginning, after a month or at most after two months, she appealed to the bishop or his envoy, saying: “I wish to be a mother; I wish to bear children, and for this reason I took a husband. But since the man I took is of a cold nature, he cannot do what I took him for,” then, if this can be established by a proper judgment, you may separate, and she may marry in the Lord if she wishes.

### Also concerning fornication

Did you commit fornication with your sister? If you did this, do penance for ten years during the prescribed penitential periods, one of those years on bread and water; for as long as you live, perform penance, and remain without hope of marriage. But your sister, if she did not consent, may, after completing her penance, marry in the Lord if she cannot remain continent.

[Col. 0967D] Did you commit fornication with your paternal or maternal aunt, or with the wife of your paternal or maternal uncle? If you did this, you must do penance for ten years during the prescribed penitential periods, one of those years on bread and water; for as long as you live, you must not be without penance, and you must remain without hope of taking a wife, unless the bishop wishes to grant you some mercy.

Did you commit fornication as the Sodomites did, inserting your penis into a male’s buttocks and anus and thus having intercourse with him in the Sodomitic manner? If you had a wife and did this once or twice, you must do penance for ten years during the prescribed penitential periods, one of those years on bread and water. If you made a habit of it, you must do penance for twelve years during the prescribed penitential periods. If you perpetrated the same crime with your blood brother, you must do penance for fifteen years during the prescribed penitential periods.

If you committed fornication with a male between the thighs, as some do—that is, if you placed your male member between another man’s thighs and, by moving it, emitted semen—if you did this, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

Did you commit fornication as some people do, namely, by taking another man’s penis in your hand and allowing him to take yours in his, and by moving each other’s penises with your hands so that, through that pleasure, you emitted semen? If you did this, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

Did you commit fornication with yourself, as some people do—that is, did you take your own male member in your hand, draw back your foreskin, and stimulate it with your own hand so that, through the pleasure, you emitted semen? If you did this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0968B] Did you commit fornication as some do, by inserting your male member into a pierced piece of wood or something similar, so that through the stimulation and pleasure you emitted semen? If you did this, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you give a woman a kiss out of unclean desire and thereby pollute yourself? If you did this, you must do penance for three days on bread and water. If this occurred inside a church, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you commit unnatural fornication—that is, did you have intercourse with males or with animals, such as a mare, cow, she-ass, or any other animal? If you did this once or twice, and did not have a wife with whom you could satisfy your lust, you must do penance for forty days on bread and water, called a *carina*, followed by seven years of penance; and never be without penance. But if you had a wife, you must do penance for ten years during the prescribed penitential periods. If you made that crime a habit, you must do penance for fifteen years during the prescribed penitential periods. If this happened to you in childhood, you must do penance for one hundred days on bread and water.

But if the offender is a slave and married, and sins with animals, then, if he is properly punished with rods, let him do penance for three years during the prescribed penitential periods. [Col. 0968D] But if the slave did this without a wife, let him likewise be punished with blows and do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods. If, however, the slave is such that he refuses to endure blows without compensation, and is a person of sufficiently high standing, let him do penance as one who is freeborn.

### Concerning illicit foods

Did you eat bodily scabs for the sake of some healing, or drink, for a purgative, little worms called lice, or drink human urine, or eat any excrement for the sake of some healing? If you did this, do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

Did you eat carrion—that is, animals torn apart by wolves or dogs and found dead in that condition? If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0969A] Did you eat birds that a hawk had struck down without first killing them with some weapon? If you did this, do penance for five days on bread and water.

Did you eat birds or animals that had been strangled in nets and were found dead in that condition? Unless you did this because of famine, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you eat a fish found dead in a river? Unless it had been handled by fishermen on that same day and had died as a result, and was found that same day—if you did this, do penance for three days on bread and water.

### Concerning fraud

Did you commit any falsification or fraud in measures or weights—that is, did you sell your goods to other Christians using a false bushel or unjust weights? If you did this or consented to it, you must do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

### Concerning incest

If you, being married, fondled the shameful parts of any woman—that is, if you fondled her breasts and genitals—if you did this, do penance for five days on bread and water. But if you were unmarried, do penance for two days on bread and water.

Did you bathe in a bathhouse with your wife and other women, and see them naked while they saw you? If you did this, you must do penance for three days on bread and water.

### Concerning hospitality

Did guests come to you in a time of necessity, and did you not receive them into your house or show them mercy, as the Lord commanded? If you failed to do this, do penance for five days on bread and water.

### Also concerning sacrilege

Did you burn down a church, or consent to its burning? If you did this, restore the church, distribute your price—that is, your *wergeld*—to the poor, and do penance for fifteen years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you retain the offerings of the dead, refusing to hand them over to the churches? If you did this, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you celebrate Easter, Pentecost, or the Nativity of the Lord somewhere other than in the city to which you are subject, except when illness prevented you? If you did this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

### Concerning the excommunicated

[Col. 0969D]

Did you knowingly have any association with an excommunicated person—that is, did you pray with him in a church or elsewhere; greet him by saying “Hail”; receive him into your house; or show him any kindness, secretly or openly, unless he wished at that same time or on that same journey to go with you for reconciliation, in which case you set him apart from the others for one or two nights, or for as long as the journey could be completed, and gave him what was necessary for food? If you acted otherwise, then you too are excommunicated in the same way as he is, and you must do penance for forty days on bread and water, called a *carina*, followed by seven years of penance.

### Concerning offerings

[Col. 0970A]

Did you withhold or retain anything from the offerings made to God—offerings in slaves, lands, woods, vineyards, utensils, clothing, and other possessions—which were undoubtedly offered to Christ, their bridegroom, through the churches, or which some faithful person left to the churches by testament? If you did this or consented to it, you must do penance for forty days on bread and water.

### Concerning tithes

Did you neglect to give God your tithe, which God himself ordained to be given to him—that is, did you fail to give him a tenth of all your produce which you wished to gather or gathered for your own use, and of all your animals; and did you exchange for a worse animal the tenth animal that you owed to God and that belonged to him? [Col. 0970B] If you did this or consented to it, first restore to God fourfold what belonged to him, and you must do penance for twenty days on bread and water.

### Also concerning robbery

Did you oppress poor people who were your neighbors and unable to defend themselves, or take their possessions against their will? If you did this, return what belongs to them and do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

### Also concerning irreligious conduct

Did you do what some people do? After lunch they go to Mass, and, being full and drunk, presume to receive from the priest the sign of peace which he offers on behalf of the people. If you did this, do penance for three days on bread and water.

Did you receive the body and blood of the Lord after tasting even the smallest amount of food? If you did this once, and did so in childhood, unless you did it as viaticum, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0970C] Did you do what some people do when they come to church? At first they barely move their lips, as though praying because of the others standing or sitting nearby, and immediately hurry off to stories and empty talk. When the priest greets them and exhorts them to prayer, they return to their stories rather than responding or praying. If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

### Concerning consent to evil

Did you conceal a brother’s sin, a sin that was mortal, and neither rebuke him nor exhort him to repent, nor come to the aid of a brother lying under a burden? If you did this, do penance for as long as you concealed it.

Did you defend the guilty out of mercy or friendship and thereby show yourself merciless toward the innocent? If you did this, do penance for thirty days on bread and water.

[Col. 0970D] Did you have Mass sung for yourself and the holy offering made while you were at home, whether in your own house or in any other place rather than in a church? If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

### Concerning unbelievers

Did you believe what some people commonly believe? When they are making a journey, if a little crow sings from their left toward their right, they hope that they will have a prosperous journey because of it. And when they are anxious about lodging, if that bird called the mouse-catcher (*muriceps*), so named because it catches mice and feeds on them, flies across the road ahead of them, they entrust themselves more to that omen and augury than to God. If you did this or believed these things, you must do penance for five days on bread and water.

Did you believe what some people commonly believe? When they need to go somewhere before daylight, they do not dare to leave, saying that the time is inauspicious, that it is not permitted to go out before the cockcrow, and that it is dangerous because unclean spirits have more power to harm before cockcrow than afterward, and because the cock is more able by its crowing to drive them away and calm them than is that divine mind which is in a human being through faith and the sign of the cross? If you did this or believed it, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you believe what some people commonly believe: that those whom the common people call the Fates—whether they exist or are able to do what is believed of them—can, when a person is born, mark him out so that whenever that person wishes he can be transformed into a wolf, which popular foolishness calls a *werewolf* (*weruvolff*), or into some other shape? If you believed that this ever happened or could happen, namely, that the divine image could be changed by anyone into another form or appearance, except by almighty God, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0971C] Did you believe what some people commonly believe: that there are wild women, whom they call woodland women (*sylvaticae*), whom they say are corporeal, who show themselves to their lovers whenever they wish, and who, they say, take pleasure with them, but whenever they wish hide themselves and vanish? If you believed this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

In all the matters mentioned above, priests must exercise great discretion, distinguishing between one who has sinned publicly and done public penance, and one who has sinned secretly and confessed voluntarily.

Although the questions stated above apply equally to women and men, the following apply specifically to women.

[Col. 0971D] Did you do what certain women commonly do at certain times of the year? Did you prepare a table in your house and place your food and drink on it, together with three knives, so that, if the three sisters whom ancient posterity and ancient foolishness called the Fates (*parcae*) should come, they might refresh themselves there? Did you thereby take away from divine mercy its power and its name and hand them over to the devil—that is, did you believe that those whom you call sisters could help you, either here or in the future? If you did this or consented to it, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do: make some device or contrivance in the shape of a male member, of whatever size you desired, and bind it with various ties in place of your own or another’s genitals, and commit fornication with other women, or allow other women to do so with you, using that instrument or another? If you did this, do penance for five years during the prescribed penitential periods.

[Col. 0972A] Did you do what certain women commonly do: with the aforementioned device or some other contrivance, did you yourself commit fornication with yourself? If you did this, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do when they wish to extinguish the lust that torments them? They join themselves together as though they should and could have intercourse, joining their genital parts to one another, and thus seek to extinguish their itching by rubbing them together. [Col. 0972B] If you did this, you must do penance for three periods of forty days during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do, committing fornication with your little son—that is, did you place your son above your indecency in order to imitate sexual intercourse? If you did this, you must do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do, submitting yourself to an animal and provoking that animal to intercourse by whatever means you could, so that it would mate with you? If you did this, do one *carina* on bread and water, followed by seven years of penance, and never be without penance.

Did you do what certain women commonly do when they fornicate and wish to kill their offspring? By their magic and herbs they cause what has been conceived in the womb to be expelled, either killing or expelling the embryo; or, if they have not yet conceived, they act so as not to conceive. If you did this, consented to it, or taught it, you must do penance for ten years during the prescribed penitential periods. But the ancient decree removes such women from the Church until the end of their lives. For whenever she has prevented conception, she will be guilty of as many homicides as conceptions prevented. Yet it makes a great difference whether she is a poor woman and acts because of the difficulty of raising a child, or whether she acts for the sake of fornication and to conceal her crime.

At the Council of Lleida, the following provision was made concerning those mentioned above who expel children conceived in adultery:

[Col. 0972D] Those who have attempted to kill children wrongly conceived and born of adultery, or who have destroyed them in their mothers’ wombs by some potion, whether male or female adulterers—that is, the father or mother—are to receive communion after the course of seven years, provided that throughout their entire lives they persist in weeping and humility.

Did you give or show something to someone so that she might expel or kill her conception? If you did this, you must do penance for seven years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you expel your conception before it had been quickened? If you did this, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods. If you did it after the conception had received a spirit, do penance for three years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you deliberately kill your son or daughter after birth? [Col. 0973A] If you did this, you must do penance for twelve years during the prescribed penitential periods and must never be without penance.

Did you neglect your infant, so that through your fault it died without baptism? If you did this, you must do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods and must never be without penance.

Did you prepare a deadly potion and kill someone with it? If you did this, you must fast for one *carina* followed by seven years of penance, and must never be without penance. But if you wished to commit the homicide and did not complete it, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you taste your husband’s semen so that, because of your diabolical practices, he might burn more passionately with love for you? If you did this, [Col. 0973B] you must do penance for seven years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you drink chrism to overturn God’s judgment, or use anything in herbs, words, wood, stone, or some foolish belief—or perform such a practice yourself, advise others to do it, hold it in your mouth, sew it into your clothing, bind it around yourself, or employ any other device so that you believed you could overturn divine judgment? If you did this, you must do penance for seven years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do and firmly believe? If their neighbor has an abundance of milk or bees, they believe that, aided by the devil through their spells and incantations, they can divert to themselves, their animals, or anyone they wish all the abundance of milk and honey that their neighbor appears to possess. [Col. 0973C] If you did this, do penance for three years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you believe what certain women commonly believe: that, whenever they enter any house, they can bewitch and destroy by word, sight, or hearing the goslings, peacocks, chicks, piglets, and offspring of other animals? If you did this or believed it, you must do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you believe what many women, turned backward toward Satan, believe and affirm to be true: that, when you have gone to bed in the silence of a troubled night, with your husband lying in your arms, you, although corporeal and with the doors closed, can go out and traverse the spaces of the earth with others deceived by the same error; kill baptized people, redeemed by the blood of Christ, without visible weapons; eat their cooked flesh; place straw, wood, or something similar in the place of their hearts; and, after eating them, make them alive again and grant them a respite of life? If you believed this, do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, followed by seven years of penance.

Did you believe what certain women commonly believe: that, together with other members of the devil, you can, in the silence of a troubled night with the doors closed, be lifted into the air as far as the clouds, fight there with others, wound others, and receive wounds from them? If you believed this, do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do? They take a live fish, put it into their genital tract, and keep it there until it dies; then, having boiled or roasted the fish, they give it to their husbands to eat, doing this so that the husbands may burn more passionately with love for them. If you did this, do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do? They lie face down and, with their buttocks uncovered, order bread to be prepared upon their naked buttocks; after it has been baked, they give it to their husbands to eat. They do this so that their husbands may burn more passionately with love for them. If you did this, do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

[Col. 0974B] Did you place your infant beside the fire, and did another person put a cauldron of water over the fire, so that the boiling water spilled over the infant and killed it? You, who were obliged to have the infant in your care for seven years, must do penance for three years during the prescribed penitential periods. But the person who put the water in the cauldron will be innocent.

Did you do what certain women do, filled with diabolical teachings? They observe and track the footprints of Christians, remove a piece of turf from their tracks, and keep it, hoping thereby to take away their health or life. If you did this or consented to it, you must do penance for five years during the prescribed penitential periods.

[Col. 0974C] Did you do what certain women commonly do? They take their menstrual blood, mix it into food or drink, and give it to their husbands to eat or drink so that they may be loved more by them. If you did this, do penance for five years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women commonly do? They take a human skull, burn it in the fire, and give the ashes to their husbands to drink for the sake of healing. If you did this, do penance for one year during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you eat or drink the blood of any animal? If you did this, do penance for five days on bread and water.

Did you do what certain women commonly do? I mean those who have crying infants: they dig into the earth, pierce it partly through, and pull the infant through the opening, saying that in this way they stop the crying of the infant. If you did this or consented to it, do penance for five days on bread and water.

Did you do what certain women commonly perform at the devil’s prompting? When an infant has died without baptism, they take the child’s corpse, place it in some hidden spot, and pierce its little body through with a stake, saying that, if they had not done this, the infant would rise and be able to harm many people. If you did this, consented to it, or believed it, you must do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you do what certain women do, filled with the devil’s audacity? When a woman is about to give birth but cannot, and dies in the pains of labor, they pierce the mother and child with a stake into the ground in the very grave. If you did this or consented to it, you must do penance for two years during the prescribed penitential periods.

Did you accidentally smother your infant, or suffocate it beneath the weight of your clothing, and did this happen after baptism? If you did this, do penance for forty days—that is, a *carina*—on bread and water, herbs, and legumes, and abstain from your spouse until those forty days have passed. Afterward, complete three years of penance and observe three Lenten periods each year. But if the infant was suffocated before baptism, do penance for the next forty days as prescribed above. Afterward, complete a five-year penance.

Did you find your infant accidentally smothered beside you, where you and your husband had lain together in bed, and did it not appear whether it had been suffocated by its father or by you, or had died a natural death? You must not therefore consider yourselves secure or be without penance. Nevertheless, in such cases great consideration must be given to mercy, where there was no evil intention but a natural death. Yet, because of negligence, you must do penance for forty days on bread and water. But if you are not unaware that you were the killers of the infant—not intentionally, but through negligence—you must do penance for three years during the prescribed penitential periods, one of those years on bread and water, and during the time of your penance you must guard yourselves from all sexual indulgence.

[Col. 0975C] Did you practice procuring prostitution, either with yourself or with others—that is, did you, in the manner of a prostitute, hand over your body to your lovers to be handled and defiled for a price; or, what is more cruel and dangerous, did you sell or surrender someone else’s body—your daughter’s, your granddaughter’s, or that of another Christian woman—to lovers; act as intermediary; or advise that some violation be committed in this manner? If you did this, do penance for six years during the prescribed penitential periods. Nevertheless, the Council of Elvira decrees that one who has committed such acts is not to receive communion except at the end of life.

Did you do what certain women commonly do? When an infant has just been born and immediately baptized, and then dies, while burying it they place a wax paten with the offering in its right hand and likewise place a wax chalice with wine in its left hand, and bury it in this manner. If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0975D] Did you do what certain adulterous women commonly do? As soon as they learn that their lovers wish to take lawful wives, they extinguish the men’s lust by some magical practice, so that the men cannot benefit their lawful wives or have intercourse with them. If you did this or taught others to do it, you must do penance for forty days on bread and water.

Did you offer your infant for baptism at a time other than the proper time—that is, on Easter Saturday or Pentecost Saturday—unless necessity due to illness required it? If you did this, you must do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Did you neglect to visit the sick, fail to go to those who were in prison, and fail to provide for them? If you failed to do this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

[Col. 0976A] Did you eat meat during Lent? If you did this, abstain from every eating of meat for the remainder of that year.

Did you eat food prepared by Jews or by other pagans for themselves? If you did this, do penance for ten days on bread and water.

Have you done what some people are accustomed to do? When they go to church, they give voice to their frivolous talk along the way and speak idle words, nor do they think on that journey about anything pertaining to the benefit of the soul. And when they have come into the church atrium, where the bodies of the faithful are buried, and while they tread upon the graves of their neighbors, they do not remember what will happen to them, nor do they make any mention or offer any prayers to the Lord for them, as they ought to have done. If you have neglected this, do penance for ten [Col. 0976B] days on bread and water, and take care that it does not happen to you again. But whenever you enter the church atrium, pray for them and ask those holy souls whose bodies rest there that they may be able to [lacuna] to the Lord for your sins in [lacuna].

Have you done any work on the Lord’s Day? If you have, you must do penance for three days on bread and water.

Have you done what certain women are accustomed to do? They remove their clothing and smear their entire naked bodies with honey. Then, with their honey-covered bodies, they repeatedly roll themselves back and forth over wheat spread on a certain cloth laid on the ground. They carefully gather all the grains of wheat that adhere to their moist bodies, put them into a mill, and cause them to go around the mill backward, against the sun, and thus grind them into flour. From that flour they make bread and give it to their husbands to eat, so that, having eaten the bread, they may waste away and perish? If you have done this, do penance for forty days on bread and water.

Have you done what certain women are accustomed to do? When they have no rain and need it, they gather a number of girls and place a little virgin as their leader. They strip her naked and lead her outside the village to a place where they find the herb henbane, which is called *belisa* in German. They make the naked girl pull up that same herb with the little finger of her right hand, and they have her tie the uprooted plant by some cord to the little toe of her right foot.
